aspects.name: A1 — Orbit-line visibility follows the station (ON in ORRERY / OFF in HELM, Settings/O override)
suspectedIssues: _orbitsUserOverride is a single session-scoped boolean that, once true, PERMANENTLY freezes visibility at the toggled value for BOTH modes — it collapses the per-mode behavior entirely. Toggle orbits off once in ORRERY, then M→HELM→M→ORRERY, and they stay off; the mode-driven default can never return without a reload. So 'orbit lines follow camera mode' only holds until the first manual toggle.

Settings/UI desync: the 'showOrbits' checkbox reflects settings.get('showOrbits') (ships false) while the mode default forces orbits ON in ORRERY — the checkbox reads unchecked while orbits are visible until the player toggles.

_applyOrbitVisibility assumes system.orbitLines / starOrbitLines / entry.moonOrbitLines all exist; confirm they are present (and empty-safe) for planetless systems, moonless planets, and binary-star orbit lines.
aspects.liveTestRecipe: Boot into ORRERY (splash ORRERY or press-anything default). After warp reveal, in the console traverse window._scene for the orbit-ring meshes (THREE.Line/LineLoop under the system group) or read the system's orbitLines and assert .visible===true; confirm document.getElementById('mode-swap-btn').textContent==='ORRERY'. Press M (swap to HELM), assert textContent==='HELM' and the same orbit meshes now have .visible===false. Press M back, assert .visible===true. Repeat the M swap 5x (BEFORE touching O) asserting orbit visibility tracks the mode each cycle. Then press O once and assert visibility flips AND that a subsequent M→HELM→M→ORRERY leaves it at the toggled value (proves the override sticks and collapses the per-mode default). Keep the window focused (rAF throttles to ~1fps when occluded).

aspects.name: In-system body + orbit-line selection (the 'plan/inspect' click)
suspectedIssues: The 'face the selected body' orbit-pivot ease (main.js:6193) is gated on !cameraController.bypassed, but ORRERY is bypassed after every warp reveal (main.js:5974) and throughout/after the autopilot tour — so in most ORRERY states the only feedback on select is the BURN button + bodyInfo, with no camera reaction.
Moons are selectable only via 3D-scene raycast, never from the minimap (SystemMap has no moon sprites).
Because selecting a body clears the warp target (and vice-versa), the plan station cannot hold a body-burn plan and a jump plan at the same time.
aspects.liveTestRecipe: In ORRERY, single-click (movement <5px) a planet in the 3D view. Assert #commit-burn-btn becomes display:block with text 'BURN → <NAME>' and the upper-left bodyInfo panel populates; window._getState()/_selectedTarget should reflect the pick. Click a thin orbit ring ~6px from any body and assert the matching planet/moon selects. Cycle select on star → planet → moon and assert the BURN label + bodyInfo update each time. In HELM (press M), aim the reticle at a body and left-click; assert it selects at the reticle (cursor hidden path).

aspects.name: A3a — Background-star / feature warp-target SELECTION (select + blink)
suspectedIssues: No stored 'this star is already the selected target' signal that the human eye or a second click could key off — which is exactly what blocks the A3 second-click affordance (next aspect).
Single-target model: picking a star clears a body plan and vice-versa (main.js:6156, 9485); intended, but means the plan station never holds both.
aspects.liveTestRecipe: In ORRERY, click empty sky near a visible background star. Assert window._warpTarget.direction is a set unit Vector3 and _warpTarget.name is populated, the green brackets blink on-screen, and bodyInfo shows the destination name. Separately call window._autoSelectWarpTarget() and assert _warpTarget populates (screensaver path). Click a body afterward and assert _warpTarget is cleared (single-selection).

aspects.name: A3b — Second-click-on-selected-star COMMITS the warp
suspectedIssues: Second-click-commit is entirely unbuilt (no code trace).

Discrepancy with the spec's 'Space still commits': a SINGLE Space does not warp — the 3-stage preview needs three Space presses (idle→preview→aligning→warp, main.js:6342/6370/6383). So the assumed baseline the A3 spec preserves is actually a multi-press preview, not a one-shot commit.

Sibling items from the SAME 2026-06-28 spec (A1 orbit lines, B1 roll, B3 remap) are built and B was Max-UAT'd 2026-06-30 — so A3 was skipped/deferred within a partially-landed spec, easy to mistake for 'done'.
aspects.liveTestRecipe: In ORRERY, click a background star (brackets blink; record window._warpTarget.direction). Click the SAME star again and MEASURE: assert NO warp starts — warpEffect stays inactive and window._getState()/window._sc show no turn/warp beginning (this confirms second-click-commit is absent). Then confirm commit still needs the Space sequence: press Space 3× (or call window._commitSelection() 3×) watching window._warpTarget/internal _portalLabState go idle→preview→aligning→warp, asserting warpEffect activates only on the 3rd. Run 3 select→triple-Space cycles to confirm the press-count is stable.

aspects.name: A2 — Click a body in ORRERY → fast (~0.3s) eased god's-eye reframe
suspectedIssues: The intended ~0.3s eased god's-eye reframe is unbuilt.
Inconsistency: the SAME planet gives different results by WHERE you click it — 3D-scene click SELECTS (no travel); minimap click flies a FULL burn. Confusing for a 'plan' station.

Half-wired ORRERY minimap burn: focusPlanet/focusStar set _flightMode=playerBurnMode() (ASSIST, main.js:6546/6595) and fly via scPilot (camera follows because the apply gate is scPilot.isActive||_scManual, main.js:7808/7873), but they do NOT set _scManual and do NOT swap to HELM. So the manual-cancel gates (manualCancelsLeg, INSIDE `if (_scManual)` at main.js:8121/8128) never fire — the ORRERY burn is uncancellable by W/S/stick, and it ends in an infinite (linger:Infinity) pilot-held orbit while the mode button still reads 'ORRERY'.
cameraController.update is skipped while scPilot.isActive (main.js:8157), so during that ORRERY minimap burn the Toy-Box orbit is fully suspended even though the station label says ORRERY.
aspects.liveTestRecipe: In ORRERY, click a planet in the 3D scene and sample window._cam / camera.position over ~1s: assert the camera does NOT translate toward the body within ~0.3s (only selection fires) — disproving A2. Then press C (minimap) and click the SAME planet: assert window._getState().speed/throttle ramp into a multi-second FULL burn and document.getElementById('mode-swap-btn').textContent stays 'ORRERY'. Mid-burn hold W then S and assert the burn does NOT cancel (speed keeps tracking the pilot; window._sc.pilot still active) — confirming the uncancellable-ORRERY-burn concern. Note there is no ~0.3s eased reframe to time; the measurement is the absence of it.

aspects.name: Minimap / System-map HUD (radar overview, drag-rotate, click-to-select/travel)
suspectedIssues: Heading pointer uses hudYaw = when cameraController.bypassed, atan2(camera.position.x, camera.position.z) (main.js:8580) — a position-angle around origin, NOT the ship's nose vector; so in HELM/flight/tour (all bypassed) the pointer heading is an approximation that can disagree with the actual heading.

Camera-position dot plots camera.position.*sceneToMap (SystemMap.js:290-292); under world-origin rebasing the camera is kept near the rebased origin, so the dot may not track the player's TRUE in-system position when far from a body (status:unknown — needs a live check).
hitTest covers stars + planets only (SystemMap.js:370-391) — no moon sprites, so you cannot select/travel to a moon from the minimap.
Minimap click TRAVELS (full burn) whereas a 3D-scene click only SELECTS (same inconsistency as A2), and the minimap-initiated ORRERY burn inherits the uncancellable-burn issue flagged under A2.
aspects.liveTestRecipe: In ORRERY press C — assert the minimap HUD appears (retroRenderer HUD = systemMap). Drag inside the minimap circle and assert the map rotates (SystemMap._mapYaw changes) without stopping the tour. Click a planet dot (non-autopilot) — assert a full burn starts (window._getState().speed ramps) and the green focus ring lands on that planet. During an autopilot tour, click a different planet dot — assert the tour retargets and travels. Fly far from origin in HELM, open the minimap, and MEASURE whether the camera dot tracks true system position or sits near map-center (resolves the rebasing-accuracy unknown). Try to click a moon on the minimap — assert nothing selects (no moon sprites). Toggle C off/on 5× — assert the HUD shows/hides each time. Verify on a planetless system that systemMap is null and C is a harmless no-op (main.js:4521).

aspects.name: Tour queue construction (per-body stop list)
suspectedIssues: No cap on queue length: a very rich system (many planets x many moons) produces a queue whose full traversal at default tourLingerMultiplier=1.0 takes ~10-20 min per cycle (each stop = align+cruise+20-39s linger). Fine for a screensaver but makes 'does a full tour complete' effectively untestable without lowering the linger multiplier.
Ordering assumes system.planets and entry.moons are populated and stable; if a planet has zero moons it is simply a single stop (fine).
aspects.liveTestRecipe: Load, let an ORRERY warp-in happen (or window._startFlythrough()). Read window._autoNav.queue — assert length === 1 (or 2 for binary) + planetCount + total moonCount, and that types run star, planet, moon..., planet, moon... in inner-to-outer order. Cross-check against window._scene traversal of the system body meshes and window._sc.controls.target.

aspects.name: Queue body-ref population (mesh + radius binding)
suspectedIssues: RELIABILITY: if any stop's bodyRef ends up null/undefined (e.g. a moon or planet whose .mesh failed to spawn), the tour-advance handler skips flyTo for that stop AND the _scLegAdvanced latch stays set (main.js:6852-6865), so the tour FREEZES permanently at the previous body — onTourComplete is never reached and the screensaver stalls. There is no null-mesh guard that skips-and-continues; it just hangs. This is the same failure class the latch comment at 6810-6818 explicitly worries about.
orbitDistance is still computed here but the supercruise pilot ignores it (it uses HOLD_VIEW_FRAC*radius); dead field that can mislead a reader into thinking framing distance is set here.
aspects.liveTestRecipe: After a tour starts, run: window._autoNav.queue.map(s=>({type:s.type, hasRef:!!s.bodyRef, r:s.bodyRadius})). Assert EVERY stop has hasRef===true and r>0. To exercise the freeze: null out one mid-queue stop's bodyRef (window._autoNav.queue[3].bodyRef=null), let the tour reach stop 2, and confirm it never advances past it (currentIndex sticks, window._sc.pilot.phase stuck HOLD).

aspects.name: Per-body tour leg motion (ALIGN to CRUISE to HOLD)
suspectedIssues: RELIABILITY (HIGH): CRUISE has NO timeout (only ALIGN does). The pilot steers straight at the target's CURRENT position through ANY intervening body. All bodies are fed to the model's collision barrier (COLLISION_FACTOR*radius) and speed cap. A tour leg whose straight line is blocked by the star (e.g. planet_i to planet_{i+1} when they are near opposite sides of the star) or by a planet occluding its own moon will WEDGE: the barrier stops forward motion, speedCap collapses, the pilot keeps aiming into the blocker, dist never falls to 10R, CRUISE never exits, motionComplete never fires — the whole screensaver freezes on that leg indefinitely. Orbital phases are independent so opposite-side geometry WILL occur over long unattended runs.

Overshoot path (149) re-loops in CRUISE with no bound; for the autopilot's own throttle (0.75) the ETA_K>=2.25 invariant makes capture speed<=cap<=4R so overshoot should essentially never fire on tour legs — but if a leg starts very hot from deep space the first pass could overshoot and loop a few times before capture.
steerToward reads the live moving body each frame (good, no stale capture), but there is no path-planning/avoidance — it is pure pursuit.
aspects.liveTestRecipe: Happy path: start a tour, watch window._sc.pilot.phase cycle ALIGN->CRUISE->HOLD per stop and window._autoNav.currentIndex increment; assert each leg reaches HOLD. Wedge probe: while touring, read star mesh pos + two planet meshes from window._scene; jump the tour to a planet currently on the far side of the star (number keys 2-9 or window._autoNav.jumpToPlanet), then poll window._sc.model.position + window._sc.model.speed for ~40s — a wedge shows phase stuck 'CRUISE', speed ~0, position frozen at ~1.05x starRadius from the star, and dist-to-target never crossing 10R. Keep the window FOCUSED (rAF throttle freezes motion when backgrounded).

aspects.name: Tour advance on arrival (HOLD linger to next leg)
suspectedIssues: If advanceToNext returns a bodyRef-less stop, flyTo is skipped but _scLegAdvanced stays true and phase never re-enters ALIGN, so the tour hangs (see queue-ref-population aspect). Level-triggered motionComplete + single latch = one-shot-or-stall by design; robust only while every stop is flyable.

The reticle/focus sync fires on the advance frame (after arrival at the NEW stop), so the 'now targeting the next body' preview that the retired flythrough mover fired ~4s BEFORE arrival (main.js:7958-7965) is absent on the supercruise tour path — a minor contemplative-reveal regression.
aspects.liveTestRecipe: Lower tourLingerMultiplier (Settings gear) to speed cycles, start a tour, and log window._autoNav.currentIndex + window._sc.pilot.phase each second. Assert currentIndex increments by 1 each time phase transitions out of HOLD, and that _scLegAdvanced (window._autoNav is separate; observe behavior) never double-advances (no skipped stops).

aspects.name: Tour completion detection + repeat within a system
suspectedIssues: Completion counting is by count only, decoupled from which stops actually got flown — if a leg silently stalls (wedge/null-ref) the counter never reaches queue.length so onTourComplete never fires and the loop dead-ends. So 'completes' is only guaranteed if every leg completes (see the two suspect aspects above).

Manual jumps via jumpTo (Tab/1-9/minimap, AutoNavigator.js:157-193) do NOT touch _stopsVisited, so heavy player interaction can make onTourComplete fire early or late relative to actual coverage — cosmetic for the unattended screensaver.
aspects.liveTestRecipe: Set tourLingerMultiplier very low. Instrument: const n=window._autoNav.queue.length; then poll window._autoNav.currentIndex and window._autoNav._stopsVisited. Assert _stopsVisited climbs 0..n-1 then wraps to 0 exactly as onTourComplete fires. Or force the terminal event directly with window._triggerTourComplete() and confirm the nav-computer overlay opens (auto-warp cinematic). Run this across >=3 systems (warp between) to confirm repeatability.

aspects.name: Tour-complete cinematic nav-computer auto-warp
suspectedIssues: The sequence is driven by wall-clock setTimeout (_delay, AutopilotNavSequence.js:648-655) but its animations use simClockMs/simRandom and its star loading depends on the nav-computer rAF render loop. For an UNATTENDED screensaver on an unfocused/background monitor, rAF throttles to ~1fps and background setTimeout is clamped to >=1s, so the 6s (20x300ms) star-load retry budget can expire before stars load -> abort -> fallback plain warp. The warp still happens (self-heals) but the intended cinematic drill-down degrades/janks exactly in the screensaver's most common runtime state.

When advanceToNext fires onTourComplete it ALSO returns the wrapped start stop, so _handleScPilotFrame dispatches a real flyTo leg toward that body that runs (hidden behind the full-screen nav overlay) concurrently with the drill-down; autoNav is only stopped when the warp dispatches, so a slow drill-down can advance the tour again in the background. Masked visually, but a latent coupling.

Sequence timers are setTimeout-based and not tied to warpEffect state; abort() is wired on stopFlythrough (main.js:5823-5826) but a mistimed manual warp during the sequence could race the pending warp dispatch.
aspects.liveTestRecipe: Force it: window._triggerTourComplete(). Assert the nav-computer overlay (#nav-computer-overlay) displays, the drill-down animates, a star is picked, and within ~30s window._getState().warp flips true (warp begins). Reliability loop: repeat window._triggerTourComplete() -> wait for warp -> new system, x5, asserting each ends in a warp. Background-throttle probe: blur the tab (or throttle rAF) during a real completion and confirm it still reaches a warp via the fallback path (console '[NAV-SEQ] No stars loaded ... Aborting' then a warp).

aspects.name: Cross-warp tour continuation into the new system
suspectedIssues: The fly-in leg is dispatched unconditionally even when _autopilotEnabled is false; in that case autoNav is inactive so _handleScPilotFrame's tour wiring returns early (6836), the ship reaches HOLD, sets _manualBurnOrbiting=true (6831-6833), and only the 300s idle timer re-engages a tour — a slow path, but not the default ORRERY flow.

Deep-sky destinations (galaxy/cluster/nebula) branch out of warpRevealSystem at 5979-6002 into a drift+linger loop with NO body tour; the loop still continues via the 15s deep-sky linger auto-warp (8054-8073), so cross-system continuation holds, just without a per-body tour for those hops.
Continuation depends on onTourComplete having fired, which depends on every leg completing (inherits the wedge/null-ref stall risks).
aspects.liveTestRecipe: From a fresh ORRERY boot, let the loop run unattended (window focused) across >=3 complete system visits. After each warp assert: window._getState().autopilot===true, window._autoNav.isActive===true, window._autoNav.queue.length>0, and document.getElementById('mode-swap-btn').textContent!=='HELM'. Confirm the destination star is in billboard LOD at emergence (per AC8) and no AC4/AC5 portal console warnings. Speed it up with a low tourLingerMultiplier and repeat >=5 cycles asserting each tour+warp completes.

aspects.name: Contemplative auto-reveal (body info + minimap focus + lingers)
suspectedIssues: No pre-arrival 'now targeting the next body' preview blink on the supercruise path (the retired flythrough mover had one at result.targetingReady, main.js:7958-7965); the reveal now happens only on arrival, so the anticipatory beat is gone.
bodyInfo/minimap reflect autoNav.getCurrentStop, but during the tour-complete overlap a hidden background leg can re-point _selectedTarget while the nav-computer overlay is up (cosmetic, hidden).
aspects.liveTestRecipe: During a tour, at each HOLD read the on-screen body-info panel and window's focusIndex/focusStarIndex/focusMoonIndex (via window._getState-adjacent state or the minimap ring) and assert they match window._autoNav.getCurrentStop() type/index. Time a few lingers with a stopwatch and confirm ~= stop.linger * tourLingerMultiplier.

aspects.name: Arrival/departure shake beats on the tour (AC6)
suspectedIssues: This sub-cluster was UAT-passed 2026-06-27 (contract.json status), so the felt beats are accepted; risk is only that the shake gate keys off pilot phase strings — if a leg wedges in CRUISE (see leg-motion aspect) the choreographer would keep signalling 'traveling' and could hold a low-level tremor indefinitely on the frozen frame.
Uses debug*Impulse entry points (debugAccelImpulse/debugDecelImpulse) as the production trigger — naming smell, not a defect.
aspects.liveTestRecipe: Ride one tour leg; sample window._sc.model.speed and shipChoreographer.shakeEuler (if exposed via window._cc or telemetry) per frame. Assert speed shows a smooth ramp on departure and a steep continuous decel into HOLD, with shakeEuler non-zero during the accel window and the 15R decel window and ~zero mid-cruise and during HOLD.

aspects.name: Deep-sky (galaxy/cluster/nebula) contemplation hop
suspectedIssues: Two linger-timer setters can race (dismissTitleScreen:2582 and drift-complete:8045 and startFlythrough:5772); warpSwapSystem resets it to -1 (5874) so stale timers are cleared, but the interplay is fiddly.
This branch has no per-body 'tour' so the reliability-critical 'tour of ALL bodies' criterion does not apply to deep-sky hops — they are a distinct loop segment.
aspects.liveTestRecipe: Force a deep-sky destination (the debug comma/period/? + Space keys per main.js:2364-2366) and warp. Assert autoNav.isActive===false, the object drifts in over ~4s, autorotate engages, and after ~15s window._getState().warp flips true (auto-warp onward). Confirm it hands back to a normal star-system tour on the next hop.

aspects.name: ORRERY orbit-line god's-eye layer
suspectedIssues: _orbitsUserOverride is sticky for the session once the player presses O, so a toured-into new system keeps the overridden state — intended, but means orbit lines can be off during a screensaver run if O was ever pressed.
Not reliability-critical to tour completion; purely visual.
aspects.liveTestRecipe: On an ORRERY warp-in (without pressing O), traverse window._scene for LineLoop orbit meshes and assert .visible===true. Press O and confirm they toggle and that a subsequent warp keeps the overridden state; check document.getElementById('mode-swap-btn').textContent!=='HELM' to confirm ORRERY.

aspects.name: Idle auto-engage of the tour
suspectedIssues: Default idleTimeout is 300s (5 min) — so if the ORRERY tour ever ends up NOT auto-started at warp-in (e.g. _autopilotEnabled false, or a stalled leg that never advances), recovery takes 5 minutes, and a wedged leg (which keeps autoNav.isActive true) is NOT recovered by the idle timer at all (the idle branch is gated on !autoNav.isActive).
So the idle timer is a re-engage safety net only for the autopilot-OFF state, not a watchdog for a stalled active tour.
aspects.liveTestRecipe: Stop the tour (Z or window._sc.controls.stop path / stopFlythrough), then leave the window untouched and focused; assert startFlythrough re-fires after idleTimeout (lower it in Settings for a fast test) by watching window._autoNav.isActive flip true. Separately confirm that with a STALLED active tour (force via null bodyRef) the idle timer does NOT recover it (gated on !isActive).

aspects.name: Boot mode-pick to first tour (ORRERY vs HELM)
suspectedIssues: _pendingBootMode is consumed once and reset to 'orrery' (6019); if warpRevealSystem's early deep-sky branch (5979) fires on the FIRST arrival (first warp lands on a galaxy/cluster), the boot-mode consumption at 6018 is never reached on that hop — HELM boot could be silently dropped for that edge (first destination is deep-sky). Low likelihood but a real ordering gap (boot-mode consume sits AFTER the deep-sky early return path in the star-system branch, but the deep-sky branch returns at 6001 before 6018).
Not a tour-completion risk for the default ORRERY-on-mobile/desktop path.
aspects.liveTestRecipe: Boot, click ORRERY, let the title auto-dismiss and first warp land; assert document.getElementById('mode-swap-btn').textContent!=='HELM', window._getState().autopilot===true, and a tour starts (window._autoNav.isActive===true). Repeat picking HELM and assert the mode button reads 'HELM' and autoNav.isActive===false. Edge: check behavior when the first destination is deep-sky.

aspects.name: Player interrupt / mid-tour jump + resume
suspectedIssues: jumpTo (AutoNavigator.js:157-162) does not reset _stopsVisited, so jumping around skews when onTourComplete fires relative to actual coverage (cosmetic for unattended runs).
_beginTourLegMotion guards on stop.bodyRef (5730) so a bad jump target no-ops rather than hangs — better than the auto-advance path, which lacks that continue-past-null behavior.
Number-key jumps only cover planets 2-9 (planetIdx 0-7) and star (1); planets beyond the 8th and moons are not directly jumpable (Tab-stepping only) — a UI limitation, not a loop breaker.
aspects.liveTestRecipe: During a tour press Tab and assert window._autoNav.currentIndex advances and window._sc.pilot.phase re-enters ALIGN toward the new body; press 1 and assert jumpToStar (currentIndex lands on the star stop). Press W and assert takeover: window._autoNav.isActive===false, mode button reads 'HELM', ship keeps its pose/speed (no snap). Press Z to confirm the tour toggles off/on.

aspects.name: Manual throttle (W/S)
suspectedIssues: NOT gated by flightOk: the `_scManual` throttle block (main.js:8121) runs whenever _scManual is true; flightOk (main.js:8111-8119, which checks settings/soundtest/keybinds-overlay open) gates only the legacy WASD else-branch. Model stepping (scActive, main.js:7808) also excludes only warp/splash/title, not overlays. So opening Settings (P) or the keybinds overlay (K) in HELM does NOT pause the ship — held W/S keeps changing throttle and the ship keeps moving. Inconsistent with the ORRERY free-flight path which DOES stop.

In supercruise, S cannot slow below MIN_CRUISE (2.0 u/s) — target is clamped to floorEff (main.js/SupercruiseModel.js:147-148). A player expecting S to stop will find it only drops to the cruise floor; the only real 'stop' is R (drop to sublight). Intended per comment but likely counter-intuitive; confirm it reads as Elite-faithful, not broken.
Reverse only exists at sublight (drive OFF). Confirm this matches intent (supercruise reverse deliberately removed, SupercruiseModel.js:145).
aspects.liveTestRecipe: Keep the window focused (rAF throttles to ~1fps when unfocused, freezing the sim). From ORRERY press R to take the Helm; assert document.getElementById('mode-swap-btn').textContent==='HELM' and window._sc.model.driveOn===true. (1) Supercruise throttle: hold W ~1.5s → sample window._sc.model.throttle rising ~0.6/s toward 1 and window._sc.model.speed exp-approaching throttle·window._sc.model.speedCap() (τ≈0.6s). Hold S back to throttle 0 → assert window._sc.model.speed floors at min(2.0, speedCap()), NOT 0. (2) Sublight reverse: press R (drop out), assert driveOn===false and speed settling toward 0; hold S ~1.5s → assert window._sc.model.throttle goes negative and window._sc.model.speed < 0. (3) Reliability: run 5 W-up/S-down cycles asserting throttle stays in [-1,1] and tracks each cycle. (4) Overlay-gate bug: in HELM press P (Settings), then hold W a moment — measure window._sc.model.throttle before/after; if it changes, the overlay-not-paused issue is confirmed.

aspects.name: Mouse virtual-joystick yaw/pitch
suspectedIssues: Absolute-position stick persists a turn when the mouse stops off-center (turnInput retains the last setTurnInput value; model.update keeps applying it) — intended Elite-style behavior, but confirm it's what Max wants vs a relative stick.

Entering free-look (F) or a middle-mouse peek does NOT zero model.turnInput.yaw/pitch. If you press F while the stick is deflected, the ship KEEPS TURNING at the frozen deflection during free-look (mousemove now routes to scHead, gate `!freeLook.latched` blocks steer). May be intended ('ship keeps flying its line', AC4) but with an absolute-position stick it means an uncommanded persistent turn while you look around; verify.

Same overlay-gate gap as throttle: steer is gated by `_scManual` (main.js:9676), not flightOk — but note it only fires on mousemove, so the practical exposure is smaller than the held-key throttle/roll.

getState()/scControls telemetry does not expose turnInput; the HUD deflection dot reflects the un-negated stick, while the applied model input is negated — confirm the reticle direction matches nose motion on screen.
aspects.liveTestRecipe: Focused window, HELM hands-on (F off — confirm window._getState() shows cursor hidden / mode-swap-btn 'HELM'). (1) Deflect right: move mouse to right edge → assert window._sc.model.turnInput.yaw < 0 (negated), |yaw|→1, and window._sc.model.orientation yaws so model.nose() rotates toward +X (nose right). Center mouse → assert turnInput.yaw→0 within the deadzone. (2) Deflect up → assert turnInput.pitch > 0 and nose pitches up. (3) Speed-dependent cap: full-deflect at near-rest, record achieved d(orientation)/dt; then throttle to near cap and full-deflect again → assert the achieved turn rate is lower (turnRateCap shrank). (4) Free-look handoff probe: deflect stick (turnInput.yaw≠0), press F, move the mouse — sample window._sc.model.turnInput.yaw over ~2s and assert whether it stays nonzero (ship keeps turning) to confirm/deny the persistence concern. (5) Reliability: 5 deflect-then-center cycles, assert turnInput returns to ~0 each time.

aspects.name: Roll axis control (Q/E)
suspectedIssues: Sign was JUST flipped to Q−E on 2026-06-30 (main.js:8138 comment) — the whole point of this cluster's 'sign just fixed' note. It has not been re-UAT'd since the flip; confirm live that Q banks LEFT and E banks RIGHT (the earlier E−Q guess shipped inverted).

turnInput.roll is written ONLY at main.js:8139 (inside `_scManual`) and is never reset on mode/regime transitions; setTurnInput(yaw,pitch) and pilot.stop() don't touch it. If Q/E are held on the exact frame you leave HELM into a running autopilot tour (scPilot.isActive && !_scManual, which still steps the model at main.js:7849), the last roll value latches and the ship rolls throughout the tour. Relies on key-release/blur to zero it.

Roll is applied unconditionally to the model even when free-look is active or the drive is dropped (it's in the _scManual poll, not gated by driveOn) — likely fine (you can roll while parked at sublight) but confirm it's intended during drop-out.
Same overlay-not-paused gap as throttle: Q/E roll runs while Settings/keybinds overlay is open in HELM.
aspects.liveTestRecipe: Focused window, HELM, MANUAL mode (Settings flightControlType default 'manual', Settings.js:63). aspects.liveTestRecipe: Set Settings → flightControlType = 'assist' (window persists to wd_ setting), enter HELM under ASSIST (M from ORRERY, or R with the assist setting). Confirm window._sc.controls.getState().mode === 'assist'. aspects.name: Sublight / supercruise drive toggle (R)
suspectedIssues: R-engage from ORRERY inherits Settings.flightControlType (main.js:8665). The big comment block at main.js:9165-9178 still narrates the OLD E-key semantics ('E key: supercruise DRIVE toggle', 'engage/dropout/reengage') immediately above the KeyR handler; only line 9179 notes the remap. Stale/misleading comment, not a runtime bug, but an easy source of future confusion.

Forced proximity drop (main.js:7841) only fires while _scManual; during an autopilot tour it relies on the pilot's HOLD-phase capture instead — confirm a manually-flown-then-handed-off approach can't slip past the horizon.

Back off and press R → succeeds. Confirm document.getElementById('mode-swap-btn').textContent === 'HELM'.

aspects.name: Flight TYPE selection (Settings) + entry dispatch (_enterFlightInternal → _enterFlightMode)
suspectedIssues: Mid-flight Settings TYPE change does NOT re-arm live — it applies only on the next E-engage (comment main.js:8661-8663).

Entering Align/Assist with nothing selected silently does nothing (_enterFlightMode returns at 6234); the mode only 'activates' when you later select a body — no toast/feedback that the assist is dormant.

The commit-burn-from-ORRERY path and the tour W/S-takeover path BYPASS _enterFlightInternal and set _flightMode directly (playerBurnMode()==ASSIST at 6546/6595/6642; MANUAL at 9272), so the Settings TYPE is ignored on those two entries — three different entry doors set _flightMode by three different rules.

aspects.name: Manual mode — hands-on baseline (you fly)
suspectedIssues: Body-frame yaw+pitch integration accumulates roll over any curved maneuver (documented B2 root cause, orrery-nav spec:44-53) — intended in Manual, but a new player sees the horizon drift with no on-screen cue that Q/E corrects it, and there is no auto-level in ANY mode to help (see roll-auto-level aspect).
Roll input at 8139 is applied whenever _scManual regardless of sub-mode, so it also injects roll during an active Assist leg without any takeover (see takeover-gates aspect).
aspects.liveTestRecipe: E to engage Manual; move mouse off canvas-center → window._sc.model.turnInput.{yaw,pitch} track deflection and the HUD reticle moves; hold W then S → window._sc.model.throttle ramps ±0.6/s; hold Q then E → turnInput.roll = ±1 and orientation rolls. Fly a sustained combined yaw+pitch arc for ~10s and confirm the horizon tilts (roll accrues) and does NOT self-correct.

aspects.name: Align-on-select (Mode B) — one-time nose ease (_alignState)
suspectedIssues: Align uses the STRICT gate ALIGN_DOT=0.995 and a short 1.5s cap (its own constants, NOT the pilot's relaxed 0.985/8s) — against a moving/orbiting body the 0.995 is often not met, so it hits the 1.5s timeout leaving the nose slightly off (silent partial-align).

W/S throttle does NOT cancel Align — only mouse-stick deflection does (cancel exists only in the mousemove handler 9696, not in the W/S block 8127); a player who nudges throttle expecting takeover keeps the align running.
Align faces yaw/pitch only; it does not level roll, and the spec's 'ALIGN folded with ASSIST → auto-level' (orrery-nav §B2) is unbuilt.

Mid-ease, deflect the mouse → assert the ease STOPS (align cancelled). Repeat and instead hold W during the ease → assert it does NOT cancel (align completes). Try Align on a fast inner moon → measure final nose-dot (expect it to hit the 1.5s cap under 0.995).

arrival-modes contract AC5 explicitly flags 'manual-cancels-Assist for the commit path UNVERIFIED via lab' — the core takeover-during-Assist behavior was never lab-verified.

'steer to take over' is weakened by the free-look redesign: a bare cursor in free-look does NOT steer (9676 gate `!freeLook.latched`), so if you launched Assist from free-look you must be hands-on (F off) or use W/S to take over.
aspects.liveTestRecipe: Settings type=Assist (or free-look aim+select+Space). Assert window._sc.pilot.phase cycles ALIGN→CRUISE→HOLD and window._sc.pilot._target.mesh stays the picked body throughout; at HOLD confirm the HUD SAFE-TO-DROP shows in-window. Then inject W → assert pilot.phase==='IDLE' and getState().mode==='manual' (takeover).

aspects.name: commit-burn-from-ORRERY becomes a HELM Assist leg
suspectedIssues: linger:Infinity → HOLD never completes (motionComplete never fires), so the burn parks forever; but HOLD entry arms _manualBurnOrbiting (6831) → the manual-burn idle timer (8017-8028) fires startFlythrough after idleTimeout → the moon-flip. A successful player Assist arrival is ALWAYS eventually yanked into a random screensaver tour (no 'deliberately parked' suppression).

This path bypasses _enterFlightInternal, so it does not clear a stranded freeLook latch, does not zero scHead, and ignores the Settings flight TYPE (forces ASSIST) — asymmetric with the E-engage door.
commitBurn from an already-HELM state does NOT swap (gate false) but still runs focus*→ASSIST from the current pose; same idle-reengage moon-flip applies.
Ship targets are excluded by design (would starve the supercruise branch); relies on commitBurnSwapsToHelm returning false for kind==='ship'.
aspects.liveTestRecipe: In ORRERY (mode-swap-btn text 'ORRERY'), open nav computer, select a planet, Space → assert document.getElementById('mode-swap-btn').textContent flips to 'HELM', window._sc.pilot.phase runs, and window._sc.pilot._target.mesh is the planet. Inject W → assert leg cancels (phase IDLE, mode manual). Separately, commit a burn, let it park at HOLD, and poll window._autoNav.isActive + window._getState() selection over time to catch the idle-reengage moon-flip (cross-ref quirk aspect).

aspects.name: Manual takeover / manual-cancel gates (manualCancelsLeg)
suspectedIssues: Roll (Q/E) is NOT a cancel trigger — the player can roll during an Assist leg without taking over; the pilot keeps steering yaw/pitch (setTurnInput ignores roll) while the ship banks, and with no B2 auto-level the bank persists. Inconsistent with W/S and stick, which DO cancel.
In free-look (latched) the mouse-stick gate is off (9676 `!freeLook.latched`), so during a free-look-launched Assist ONLY W/S can take over — stick-deflection takeover is impossible while latched.
Two separate takeover code paths (Assist gate vs tour autoNav branch) that must stay in lock-step; arrival-modes AC5 marks the commit-path takeover UNVERIFIED.
Both gates require _scManual; a subtle mismatch (e.g. an Assist leg where _scManual got cleared) would make the leg uncancellable — the exact pre-fix bug playerBurnMode() was created to prevent.
aspects.liveTestRecipe: Launch an Assist leg (previous aspects). While window._sc.pilot.phase is CRUISE: (i) press W → assert phase IDLE + getState().mode 'manual'; repeat fresh legs with S, and with hands-on mouse-stick deflection (F off). (ii) On a fresh leg press ONLY Q/E → assert phase UNCHANGED and window._sc.model.turnInput.roll !== 0 (documents non-cancel). (iii) On a fresh leg press F (free-look) then deflect mouse → assert phase unchanged (stick gated); then W → assert takeover.

aspects.name: Per-mode roll auto-level (B2) — DEFERRED / NOT BUILT
suspectedIssues: ASSIST auto-level (roll-spec AC6) is entirely absent — an Assist leg that accumulates roll (or takes a stray Q/E) is never corrected; the assisted regime still has the exact horizon-tilt annoyance the spec set out to kill.
ALIGN auto-level (folded-with-Assist) also absent.
The world-+Y level reference, forward‖up degeneracy skip, and gentle-gain corrector described in §B2 do not exist anywhere.

Verify the roll-spec's other ACs shipped: the keybinds overlay should reflect Q/E=roll, R=drive, C=minimap, Z=tour (B3 remap IS in code at 8139/9180/9155/9253) — confirm the on-screen keybind text was updated too.
aspects.liveTestRecipe: Settings type=Assist, launch an Assist leg; use Q/E to bank ~30°, then RELEASE all keys. Assert window._sc.model.turnInput.roll returns to 0 (input-driven) BUT the ship's local up vector does NOT re-converge to world +Y over ~5s (measure ship-up · +Y — expect it to stay tilted). Repeat in MANUAL (same result, expected by design). Both confirm auto-level is unbuilt. Also open the keybinds overlay (K) and confirm it lists Q/E roll, R drive, Z tour, C minimap.

aspects.name: Assist ~55s non-convergence + auto-flip-to-a-moon quirk
suspectedIssues: NOW.md:681-682 still lists the quirk as live/deferred AFTER the AC8 ALIGN fix landed and went unit-green — so the residual is NOT the ALIGN gate; it is CRUISE (no target-lead) failing to capture a small/fast-orbiting moon and/or the idle-reengage re-targeting.

The pilot NEVER changes its own _target (the align test asserts pilot._target.mesh is stable) — the 'flip to a moon' is the SELECTION-LAYER idle screensaver re-engage (startFlythrough random stop), not the pilot. Conflating the two (as the spec's Feature-6 diagnosis does) hides the real cause.

idleTimeout default is 300s (src/ui/Settings.js:16); a ~55s observation implies a lower saved idleTimeout, a faster path (_engageAssist linger 8 + short idle), or an approximate observation — needs live timing to pin.
No suppression of the idle-reengage while the player is deliberately parked at their Assist target — every successful Assist arrival eventually gets yanked into a random tour.

CRUISE_THROTTLE 0.75 vs the tiny dropMaxSpeed (4R) for small moons can produce a repeated-overshoot limit cycle (frame.overshoot, SupercruisePilot.js:149) — genuine non-convergence distinct from the ALIGN gate.
aspects.liveTestRecipe: Load Solar system (Shift+L teleports near the Moon; or nav to Saturn/Dione). Launch an Assist leg to a moon (or to a planet and let it park). Poll every 1s: window._sc.pilot.phase, window._sc.pilot._target?.mesh, window._autoNav.isActive, and the current selection via window._getState(). MEASURE (repeat N=10 across moons): (i) time-to-HOLD with zero target change — flag any leg that never reaches HOLD (CRUISE limit-cycle / non-convergence, target a fast small inner moon to provoke it); (ii) after HOLD, elapsed until window._autoNav.isActive flips true AND the selected target changes to a different body — that elapsed is the moon-flip; compare it against settings.get('idleTimeout') to confirm the idle-reengage is the mechanism. To isolate part A from part B, temporarily set a huge idleTimeout in Settings and confirm the flip disappears while non-convergence (if any) remains.

aspects.name: Hard collision barrier (never fly through a body)
suspectedIssues: Single-pass, at-most-one-body assumption: comment claims 'bodies don't overlap' so only one barrier fires per tick, but moons orbit close to their planet; if a moon's 1.05R barrier overlaps the planet's 1.05R barrier the loop corrects only the last-violated body per tick — could leave the ship momentarily inside the other's barrier (self-heals over subsequent ticks, but unverified).

Only bodies pushed into _scBodies are guarded — rings, asteroid belts, station/ship props, and any non-star/planet/moon geometry are NOT collidable (you can fly through them). Consistent with rings being explicitly non-traversable-but-non-collidable elsewhere, but worth confirming nothing solid is missing.

AUTOPILOT DEADLOCK RISK: the barrier converts 'fly through' into 'stop dead at surface', but the autopilot pilot (SupercruisePilot.js CRUISE) steers in a straight line at the TARGET body with no obstacle avoidance and no forced-drop (that is manual-only). A tour leg whose straight path crosses the central star would jam the ship against the star's 1.05R barrier (speed zeroed each tick, nose still pointed through the star) with no CRUISE timeout to recover. This is the most likely way the 'safety' feature actively breaks the screensaver.

No swept-collision / continuous test — only the post-step final position is checked. Static analysis says per-tick displacement stays far below the barrier gap because speedCap clamps speed to surfaceDist/ETA_K BEFORE translating (so you decelerate into any body), but there is no unit test for the high-speed (deep-space CAP_MAX=20000 u/s) approach to a very small moon; confirm no tunneling there.
aspects.liveTestRecipe: Keep the window focused (rAF throttles to ~1fps when occluded, freezing motion). 1) Enter HELM hands-on and engage the drive (R). 2) Point the nose straight at a planet (mouse-as-stick) and hold W to full throttle. Poll window._sc.model.position.distanceTo(planetMesh.position) and window._sc.model.speed each ~250ms; assert distance never drops below 1.05 × planet radius and that speed snaps to 0 at the barrier. (Planet radius: window._sc.model._bodies[i].radius; planet mesh pos via window._scene traverse or window._getState().) 3) Rotate 180° and throttle forward — assert distance increases (can leave). 4) Degenerate check: in console set window._sc.model.position.copy(planetMesh.position) then window._sc.model.update(1/60); assert position is finite and distance ≈ 1.05R. 5) AUTOPILOT DEADLOCK LOOP: run N≥6 warp+full-tour cycles (window._autoSelectWarpTarget(); window._commitSelection(); window._beginWarpTurn(); then let window._autoNav run the whole tour). For each leg watch window._sc.pilot.phase and window._sc.model.speed; assert no leg sits with speed pinned near 0 while phase stays CRUISE for >5s (that signature = jammed on the star) and every leg reaches HOLD then motionComplete.

aspects.name: Mass-based forced drop-out near mass (direction-aware)
suspectedIssues: Manual-flight-only by design (gated on _scManual) — the AUTOPILOT gets NO forced-drop. So the 'stars push you out far' safety only protects the player; the screensaver tour relies purely on the 1.05R collision barrier, which is the deadlock vector noted in the collision-barrier aspect. This split is intentional per spec but means the star-standoff guarantee is half the system.

Star mass is re-derived from RENDERED radius via massSolar=radiusSolar^1.25 (proximityHorizon.js:19-23), not the generator's persisted starMassSolar (which was thrown away — grounding map §1). Spec §8 flags this as tolerable-but-approximate; the horizon distance can differ slightly from a 'true' mass. Fine for a tunable safety net, but it means the forced-drop radius is derived from a visual quantity.

v_ref for the horizon is hard-coupled to SUBLIGHT_CAP (proximityHorizon uses it directly, SupercruiseModel.js:103). Retuning sublight top speed silently moves every star's force-drop radius. Spec §8 acknowledges and defers splitting a HORIZON_REF_SPEED constant.

Direction-awareness uses instantaneous nose dot, not velocity — a ship drifting inbound with the nose already swung away would NOT force-drop even though it is still closing on the star (Max explicitly chose nose-direction over velocity-aware; spec Out-of-scope). Combined with no real gravity pull, you could coast inbound past the horizon.

The forced-drop fires only while driveOn; once dropped it won't re-fire, but nothing prevents sublight-flying from the ~4.2R horizon all the way to the 1.05R star surface (spec §8 'stars are a hassle zone' — intended, but no heat/damage means there is no actual penalty).
aspects.liveTestRecipe: Focused window, HELM hands-on, in Sol (known G star). 1) Engage drive (R), point nose directly at the star, hold W. Poll window._sc.model.driveOn and window._sc.model.position.distanceTo(starMesh.position); assert driveOn flips true→false at distance ≈ 4.2 × star radius (read star radius = the _bodies entry with a massKg field, window._sc.model._bodies.find(b=>b.massKg).radius), and that console logged '[MODE] forced proximity drop'. 2) Repeat but with nose pointed 90°/away while inside 4.2R: assert driveOn STAYS true (window._sc.model.proximityDropRequired() returns false) and you can throttle away — distance increases. 3) Planet floor: nose-in on a planet, assert force-drop fires only at ≈1.1 × planet radius, not the star's larger multiple. 4) Autopilot gap check: during an autopilot leg (window._sc.pilot.isActive true, _scManual false) fly the tour past the star and confirm NO force-drop occurs (driveOn stays ON) — documents the manual-only scope. Reliability: repeat the head-on approach 5×, assert force-drop radius is stable within ±5%.

aspects.name: Mass-lock re-engage block + TOO CLOSE hint
suspectedIssues: The 90-frame (~1.5s) hint countdown at main.js:7847 lives inside the scActive block (requires !warpEffect && !splash && !title). Normally true when parked in flight, but if some transition clears scActive the counter freezes rather than counting down — cosmetic only.

The 'engage' branch (from Toybox, main.js:9189-9193) and the 'dropout' branch do NOT check proximityDropRequired — only 'reengage' does. Entering flight fresh (E/R from Toybox) near a star could immediately engage then be force-dropped next tick by the manual forced-drop path (a one-frame flicker), since the mass-lock guard only protects the reengage transition. Spec intended the guard specifically to kill that flicker, but only wired it on reengage.
Block relies entirely on proximityDropRequired's nose-direction test — same instantaneous-heading limitation as the forced-drop; a nose-away reengage is allowed even if drifting inbound.
aspects.liveTestRecipe: Focused window, HELM hands-on in Sol. 1) Sublight in to within ~3R of the star nose-first (drive gets force-dropped). 2) With nose still toward the star, press R (reengage). Assert: window._sc.model.driveOn stays false, console logs 'reengage blocked — mass-locked', and 'TOO CLOSE — SUBLIGHT ONLY' appears (read window._sc HUD or SupercruiseHud.getLastFrameState()/DOM) for ~1.5s. 3) Turn the nose away from the star, press R again. Assert driveOn flips to true (no soft-lock) and you accelerate away — confirms the direction-aware escape hatch. 4) Flicker probe: from Toybox near a star, press R to engage while nosed at the star; watch whether driveOn engages then force-drops within a few frames (documents the engage-branch gap).

aspects.name: proximityHorizon escape-velocity math + star-mass rederivation
suspectedIssues: ^1.25 rederivation from the RENDERED radius is an approximation of the generator's own starMassSolar (which is computed from radiusSolarVaried, not the final rendered radius) — spec §8 flags a possible small mismatch; acceptable for a tunable safety distance but it is a derived-from-visual quantity, not ground truth.

The helper is only correct for stars; if a caller ever attaches massKg to a planet/moon push in _scBodies the horizon would be computed with the star relation (^1.25 solar) against a planet radius — currently avoided only by convention (main.js pushes massKg on star lines 7817/7821 only). No guard in the helper itself.
Binary star2 also gets massKg (main.js:7821-7822) so both stars produce horizons — correct, but untested for the binary case (proximityHorizon.test.js only covers a single star).
aspects.liveTestRecipe: Mostly headless-verifiable but confirm live in-app: in console call window._sc.model._bodies.filter(b=>b.massKg) after entering a system — assert exactly the star(s) carry massKg and the value ≈1.989e30 for a 1 R☉ star. Compute window._sc.tuning.SUBLIGHT_CAP and verify the observed force-drop radius from the forced-drop test (~4.2R) matches forcedDropRadiusScene(massKg, SUBLIGHT_CAP)/starRadius. For a binary, repeat and confirm BOTH stars produce a nonzero horizon (fly toward each, assert force-drop at each). No repeat loop needed — pure math, but re-run across 3 different star classes (small red dwarf, G, large giant) and assert horizon multiple grows with radius.

aspects.name: Minimum-cruise floor + gravity-well speed cap (slow-near-mass / anti-clip)
suspectedIssues: MIN_CRUISE clamp removes reverse and stop WHILE drive-ON (target clamped ≥ floorEff > 0) — intended ('can't crawl/stop in supercruise') but means a player who wants to hold position must drop to sublight; the only sub-floor motion is a gravity well forcing you down (floorEff yields to cap) or dropping out.

The CAP_MIN_FRAC floor keeps the near-body cap at 0.5R (not ~0), so the model's 'anti-clip: engage into a body can't exceed ~0' comment (line 163-164) is slightly optimistic — you can still move at up to 0.5R/60 per tick into a surface; it is the separate 1.05R collision barrier (176-189), not the cap alone, that actually prevents penetration. Anti-clip is a two-mechanism story; the cap only guarantees the per-tick step stays small enough for the barrier to catch.

ETA_K=3.0 must stay ≥2.25 for drop-safety (capture sphere speed ≤ dropMax); tuned down from 6→3 for feel (comment line 11-13). Any further live retune below 2.25 silently breaks capturability — no runtime assertion guards this invariant.

The tuning comment budget (SUBLIGHT_TAU ≤ ETA_K/4, ACCEL_TAU ≤ ETA_K/4) is documentation-only; nothing enforces it, so live-dialing SUBLIGHT_CAP/ETA_K via window._sc.tuning could produce underdamped surging or unsafe capture with no warning.

No unit test asserts monotonic increase of the cap with distance across multiple bodies or the multi-body min selection under motion; AC1's 'monotonically increasing cap' is claimed green but re-confirm the min-over-bodies picks the nearest correctly when two bodies are comparably close.
aspects.liveTestRecipe: Focused window. 1) Deep space: in HELM with drive ON far from all bodies, full throttle; assert window._sc.model.speed approaches ~throttle×CAP_MAX and window._sc.model.speedCap() ≈ 20000. 2) Approach a planet nose-first at cruise; log speedCap() and speed each 250ms — assert speedCap decreases monotonically as distance shrinks and speed tracks it down (the Elite decel-on-approach), never exceeding cap. 3) Min-cruise floor: near a body reduce throttle to 0 (S then release), assert speed does NOT drop below min(2.0, speedCap()) while driveOn true; then drop out (R) and assert sublight now allows full stop (throttle 0 → speed→0). 4) Anti-clip integration: at full deep-space speed aim at a small moon and hold W; assert speed is clamped down by the cap before reaching it AND the collision barrier catches you at 1.05R (distance never < 1.05×moon radius, speed→0) — no tunneling. 5) Turn-authority coupling: at high speed vs near-rest, apply equal stick and compare achieved turn rate (window._sc.model.turnRateCap()); assert high-speed cap < low-speed cap. Reliability: run steps 2+4 across a small moon and a large planet to confirm scale-free behavior.

aspects.name: trySelectWarpTarget — background-star pick + destination routing

aspects.name: WarpEffect FOLD/ENTER/HYPER/EXIT state machine + load-adaptive HYPER
suspectedIssues: Two independent onSwapSystem triggers exist: the geometric Portal-A crossing (main.js:1976) and the HYPER fallback timer (WarpEffect.js:310). Both gate on !_swapFired so only one fires, but if the geometric crossing NEVER fires (off-axis miss), the timer path swaps WITHOUT the camera being INSIDE — the AC10 occlusion guard (main.js:3477) would then log '[WARP][AC10] swap exposed!' but only warns; the teleport could be briefly visible.

safetyCeiling = HYPER_DUR×4 = 12s (323): if destinationReady never sets (compileAsync hang) AND the emergence crossing never fires, HYPER hard-exits at 12s and onComplete force-flips OUTSIDE_B (3667) — player emerges into a possibly-half-loaded system. This is the designed no-hang backstop, but it masks the real failure as a silent 12s pause.

warpSwapSystem's camera-placement math (5887-5896) hard-codes speed=80 and FOLD/ENTER/HYPER/EXIT distances that must stay in sync with WarpEffect's actual speed ramps; these are duplicated constants (foldDist=53, enterDist=90, hyperDist=speed×HYPER_DUR) that will silently drift if the ramp shapes or durations change.
aspects.liveTestRecipe: Front window; enable ?warpDebug (window._warpDebugHUD panel) or read window._warpEffect. enterSol(); auto-select + begin a warp; sample window._warpEffect.state + .progress each ~0.5s and assert the sequence fold→enter→hyper→exit→idle with elapsed roughly 4/1.5/≥3.5/2s. To exercise load-adaptive HYPER, set a slow-load by inspecting window.__swapTiming after arrival (compileMs) — on a genuinely slow compile assert HYPER elapsed exceeds HYPER_MIN_CRUISE (3.5) before exit. Watch console for any '[WARP][AC10] swap exposed' or '[WARP][AC4] onComplete reached still INSIDE' — either indicates the geometric path failed.

aspects.name: warpPortal ENTRY traversal — OUTSIDE_A→INSIDE crossing + Fix D on-axis advance (HISTORICALLY FLAKY)
suspectedIssues: Documented residual: even after Fix D, live runs showed ~10/12 registering with a residual ~2/12 miss on deep consecutive warps (memory finding #4, 'turn-alignment accumulation, mechanism not yet pinned', DEFERRED). The task's '~7 warps then degrades' is this tail. Current code advances along _tunnelForward which SHOULD make entry facing-independent, so if misses persist the cause is elsewhere (portal placement vs camera, or interp resync) — unresolved and untested since the code evolved past the memory (memory says _advanceDir uses _sunDir post-swap; code now uses _destForward, 7676).

renderFrame/simStep split: updateTraversal (renderFrame, 8428) calls group/disc updateMatrixWorld, but the AC5 clamp in simStep reads warpPortal._discB.matrixWorld (7706) with a comment claiming 'matrixWorld is current — updateTraversal refreshed it this frame' — that ordering claim predates the 2026-06-10 move of updateTraversal to renderFrame. In simStep the disc matrix can be one render-frame stale relative to the 7536 group-position rewrite, giving a slightly-off axisToB for the clamp.

Portal A is opened at FOLD t=0 from the LIVE camera position (7516), but during the manual 3-stage path the portal was ALREADY opened at preview time (6356) and _openedThisWarp gates re-opening; the resetTraversal in the FOLD block (7518) only runs when it re-opens. Need to confirm the preview portal and the FOLD portal agree in position (they should, camera hasn't moved) — no assertion guards a drift.
The 3u gate is generous but fixed; a warp whose _tunnelForward and camera path diverge (stale-target re-select edge, or a rebase mid-FOLD) could still lat-reject.

aspects.name: onSwapSystem — mid-cruise teleport, rebase-proof pocket re-anchor, AC5 emergence clamp
suspectedIssues: This is the most fragile, race-prone node in the pipeline: async teleport vs the fixed-timestep sim vs world-origin rebasing. The 0.5u back-margin (3526) is explicitly tuned against float64 noise at destination magnitudes 1e4-1e6 (a smaller margin fired spurious INSIDE→OUTSIDE_A 'backed out'); a far-enough destination (galactic-scale, worldOrigin ~6M) could still push dotA into noise — pinned only by tests/portal-traversal-margin.test.js, not asserted live.
AC10 guard (3479) is warn-only console.error — if a future movement change exposes the ~3000u teleport it logs but does not prevent the visible jump.

Two onSwapSystem callers (geometric 1976 + HYPER timer 312) both re-anchor now, but the re-anchor lives in onSwapSystem body; if only the timer fires (geometric miss), the camera was NOT actually INSIDE at teleport → AC10 warns and Portal B may not be crossable, cascading to the onComplete force-flip.
The AC5 clamp reads _discB.matrixWorld in simStep (7706) — same one-frame-stale concern as the ENTRY aspect (updateTraversal that refreshes it now runs in renderFrame).

_parkEntryDepth caps parkBackDepth's start so the hold isn't behind the camera (7708); if the swap drops the camera shallower than minBack (6u), the clamp math Math.max(0, axisToB−parkBackEff) can pin _step to 0 and momentarily freeze forward progress until the ease catches up — the very 'freeze' the soft-creep was meant to avoid, at the shallow-entry extreme.
compileAsync failure only warns and continues (3629); a partial compile still flips destinationReady=true (3637) → emergence into an un-compiled system with a first-frame sync-link hitch.

During HYPER, poll window._warpPortal._traversalMode (should be 'INSIDE') and window._warpEffect.state ('hyper'); assert no '[WARP][AC10] swap exposed' in console. aspects.name: warpPortal EMERGENCE — INSIDE→OUTSIDE_B crossing drives EXIT + AC8 close-tween
suspectedIssues: The onComplete force-flip fallback (3667) existing at all means the emergence crossing is not guaranteed — when the safety ceiling or a Portal-B miss occurs, emergence degrades to exactly the 'freeze-then-snap' the redesign was meant to kill (spec §1 failure). Frequency is unmeasured in current code; the console.warn is the only signal.

Portal B is the FAR/pinched end (FAR_TAPER 0.12, WarpPortal.js:120) but the emergence gate uses the fixed 3u _gateRadiusScene, not the tapered mesh radius (857-862) — intentional (gate ≠ visual), but it means the visible throat is far narrower than the crossing gate; a camera slightly off the axis crosses the gate while appearing to clip the tapered wall.

The close-tween spans EXIT(~2s)+~1s coast and is driven in BOTH the warp-active block (7552) and the post-warp else block (7767); if onComplete's force-flip path starts a SECOND startClose while one is already running, _closeT resets to 0 (717) restarting the fade — a double-start could visibly re-open then re-close.

AC7 says the portal is frozen at its true-world exit anchor with NO camera follow post-warp (7751-7759); this relies on maybeRebase carrying the scene-child correctly — if a rebase lands mid-close the frozen ring could jump.

After arrival, scan the trace for a record where prevMode==='INSIDE' and mode==='OUTSIDE_B' (the emergence crossing) — assert it exists and occurred BEFORE warpEffect reached 'idle'. aspects.name: warpRevealSystem — system reveal, boot-mode consumption, orbit sync, tour/HELM handoff
suspectedIssues: Boot pick is consumed ONLY on the star-system path (6018); if the very first post-boot warp lands on DEEP SKY (feature/galaxy) the deep-sky branch returns at 6001 BEFORE consuming _pendingBootMode, so a HELM pick would silently carry to the next star-system reveal — an unlikely but real ordering gap (title→warp normally targets a star, but auto/nav paths can pick features).

The fly-in seam comment (6040-6047) asserts 'the pilot is never active here (beginWarpTurn stops it… warpSwapSystem stops it defensively)'; correctness depends on BOTH stops having run — if a warp reached reveal via a path that skipped both (none obvious today), _seedScPoseFromCameraIfIdle's guard is the only protection.

HELM boot enters flight from the warp-exit pose with the drive left untouched (6017 comment); if the arrival distance/orientation from warpSwapSystem is off, the player starts flight facing away from the star.

Orbit realism here is only visibility sync (_syncOrbitsToMode, 6033); actual procedural orbit geometry is spawnSystem's job (outside this function) — reveal just toggles line meshes, so 'procedural orbit realism' is not validated at reveal time.

aspects.name: Repeat-warp reliability loop — select→warp→arrive, REPEATEDLY (screensaver + manual)
suspectedIssues: The primary open reliability risk in the whole cluster: memory well-dipper-warp-entry-rootcause finding #4 — a PROGRESSIVE degradation (fresh 7/7 register → after ~7 warps 12/12 miss pre-Fix-D; 10/12 post-Fix-D) whose MECHANISM WAS NEVER PINNED and is explicitly DEFERRED. Some accumulated per-warp state breaks entry over a long loop; candidates not ruled out: cameraInterp resync drift, worldOrigin rebase interaction across many teleports, or scPilot/autoNav residue. Unresolved and the exact thing the task flags.

Multiple reset flags must ALL fire every cycle (_openedThisWarp, _swapFired, destinationReady, _parkEntryDepth, _swapGatedRoots, traversal dot history, warpTarget). onComplete is the single point that clears _openedThisWarp and defensively restores gated roots — if a warp exits via the safety ceiling with compileAsync still pending, onComplete's defensive restore runs (3652) but any missed flag would stale the NEXT warp (e.g. a leftover-visible Portal B was the original repeat-warp orphan, spec §1).
The screensaver loop uses the beginWarpTurn TURN path (3s-timeout-prone), not the manual 3-stage preview, so the loop inherits beginWarpTurn's off-axis-fire risk on every unattended cycle.
billboard-distance arrival (AC8) depends on warpSwapSystem's switchDist math (5930-5940); a wide binary or unusual star could emerge outside billboard LOD, which the loop does not self-correct.
aspects.liveTestRecipe: Front the GPU window and VERIFY rAF fps first (an occluded window fakes freezes/misses — select_page bringToFront). Run the built regression harness: window.__wd.runWarpEntrySuite({warps: 20}) from a single enterSol WITHOUT reload; assert 20/20 report insideFlip and a real OUTSIDE_B emergence, and specifically watch warps 7-20 for the degradation tail. Separately drive the FULL screensaver loop: enterSol, enable autopilot, and let it run ≥15 unattended cycles (tour→warp→arrive), asserting each: window._warpEffect reaches 'idle' in a fresh system, no console '[WARP]' AC4/AC10 warnings, no black HYPER frame (screenshot mid-HYPER shows tunnel walls), destination star in billboard LOD at emergence, and _portalLabState stays 'idle' between warps. Capture window.__swapTiming each cycle to catch a creeping compile/teleport cost.

aspects.name: ShipCameraSystem — TOY_BOX god's-eye orbit (ORRERY)
suspectedIssues: During the normal screensaver ORRERY tour the orbit code is NOT what you see — the supercruise pilot (scPilot.isActive) owns the camera the whole tour incl. the HOLD linger, so cameraController.update is skipped. The TOY_BOX orbit only actually drives the camera once the pilot is idle AND _scManual is false (e.g. after stopFlythrough/Z, deep-sky, or a manual-burn that isn't running). Easy to misattribute tour framing to this code.
trackTarget()'s free-look branch (601-621) mutates camera.position directly by body-delta; only reachable via the legacy isFreeLooking path, not the HeadMount free-look.
aspects.liveTestRecipe: Load, let the intro warp into a star system, press Z to stop the tour (stopFlythrough → restoreFromWorldState, bypassed=false, _scManual=false, scPilot idle). Confirm document.getElementById('mode-swap-btn').textContent==='ORRERY'. Drag LMB: window._cam.quaternion changes smoothly (assert window._cc.isFlightMode===false, window._cc.cameraMode==='toy_box'). Scroll: window._cc.distance changes. Watch a focused planet stay centered over ~10s (trackTarget). aspects.name: ShipCameraSystem — legacy FLIGHT mode (FlightDynamics + CinematicDirector)
suspectedIssues: RESURRECTABLE DEAD PATH: cameraMode is persisted to localStorage 'wd_cameraMode' (ShipCameraSystem.js:437). _enterFlightInternal persists 'flight' on HELM entry. If the player quits while in HELM, localStorage='flight', and on next boot _loadPersistedMode (428-435) sets cameraMode=FLIGHT. NOTHING on the ORRERY boot/reveal path forces setCameraMode(TOY_BOX) (only _exitFlightInternal:8686 does). So after boot into the ORRERY screensaver tour, if the tour is stopped (Z→stopFlythrough), scPilot goes idle, _scManual=false, restoreFromWorldState sets bypassed=false AND syncs flight.position to camera (702), and the next cameraController.update runs the FLIGHT branch → CinematicDirector composes a chase offset → the camera JUMPS to a chase shot. This directly violates 'correct camera per mode; no snaps on transitions'.

The FLIGHT-branch look-offset/chaseScale/WASD-thrust machinery (setFlightInput 774-812, _decayLookOffset, _applyLookOffset) is all dead in the supercruise build but still allocates state and is documented as live — maintenance/comprehension hazard.

FrameDiagnostics.flightDiverge (ShipCameraSystem.js:129-138) only measures against the FLIGHT branch's expected write; it never runs during supercruise HELM (update skipped), so the diagnostic gives no coverage of the live pose path.

Let the intro warp complete into a star system, then press Z to stop the tour. MEASURE window._cc.cameraMode (expect 'flight'), window._cc.isFlightMode (expect true), and capture window._cam.position before/after the stop frame — assert whether the camera jumps (bug) vs stays put. Also assert window._cc._diagnostics.getSummary() shows JUMP. Contrast: localStorage.setItem('wd_cameraMode','toy_box'); reload; repeat — expect no jump. aspects.name: Supercruise camera pose write (scHead.applyTo in simStep)
suspectedIssues: The pose write happens in simStep (fixed 60Hz) and the render frame interpolates (cameraInterp.applyTo, main.js:8399-8400). The rAF-throttle caveat means an unfocused/occluded window freezes motion at ~1fps — any live measurement MUST keep the tab focused/visible or the pose write appears frozen.

aspects.name: HeadMount — yaw/pitch free-look + roll-carry via model.orientation
suspectedIssues: ROLL SNAP ON EXIT: if the player rolls the ship with Q/E and then leaves HELM (F is not exit anymore, but M/mode-swap → _exitFlightInternal), the no-snap exit uses camera.getWorldDirection()+adoptCurrentPose→_applyOrbit→camera.lookAt(target) with camera.up=(0,1,0) (ShipCameraSystem.js:509-518,517), which RE-LEVELS the horizon. Position and look-direction are preserved but ROLL is discarded — a visible roll snap to level on HELM→ORRERY exit when the ship was rolled. Q/E roll was only added 2026-06-30, likely untested against the exit path.
Free-look yaw/pitch are applied in the ROLLED frame (shipQuat×look), so while rolled the look axes are tilted — arguably correct (head-in-cockpit) but may feel off; worth an eyeball.
MAX_YAW=135° means you can look well behind the wings; combined with the joystick gate freezing while held, verify the transition back to steering after a wide look isn't disorienting.
No roll clamp/normalization guard beyond quaternion.normalize() each tick — sustained Q/E can accumulate arbitrary roll with no auto-level; intended, but note there is no 'level horizon' assist.

Now press M (swap to ORRERY) and capture window._cam.quaternion the frame before and after: assert whether roll snaps to 0 (bug) or is preserved/eased. Separately test free-look: F on, LMB-drag right+up, release (view HOLDS — assert window._sc.head.yaw/pitch stay non-zero and unchanged after release), then F off and sample window._sc.head.yaw/pitch decaying to 0 over ~0.5s (EXIT_RECENTER_TAU=0.18). Reliability: 5× roll-then-M cycles, log max quat-dot discontinuity.

aspects.name: freeLook latch + freeLookApply recenter bridge
suspectedIssues: STALE recenterPending across mode-swap: _doModeSwap calls freeLook.exit() (sets recenterPending=true) THEN _exitFlightInternal, but the frame bridge stops running once you leave HELM, so recenterPending is never consumed and never cleared. On the NEXT HELM entry the first bridge frame consumes a stale recenter → beginRecenter, but head yaw/pitch were reset to 0 on exit (main.js:8730-8731) so it is a no-op. Harmless today, but it is unclean latch state that could bite if exit stops zeroing the head.

F-off recenter only eases while the frame loop still applies the head (scPilot.isActive || _scManual). If you F-off in the exact frame you also leave flight, the recenter is dropped (view left wherever it was until the exit zeroes it). The two paths (F-off recenter vs M-swap adopt-current-pose) treat a held look differently — F-off eases to nose, M-swap bakes the looked-away direction as the orbit forward. Verify both read as intended 'no snap'.

freeLook is available during the autopilot TOUR (scPilot.isActive), so F during the screensaver latches free-look while the pilot flies; confirm the joystick gate (!freeLook.latched) and pilot steering don't interfere.

LMB-drag to look, release — assert window._sc.head.yaw persists (HOLD). Move the bare cursor (no button) and assert window._sc.head.yaw is UNCHANGED and window._sc.model.turnInput stays 0 (free pointer neither looks nor steers).
