aspects.name: No-snap flight-exit anchor (flightExitAnchor + adoptCurrentPose)
suspectedIssues: Roll is NOT preserved by this exit (see HeadMount aspect): camera.lookAt re-levels, so exiting while rolled snaps the horizon — the position/look-dir contract holds but roll is silently dropped.

The commit-burn-from-ORRERY→HELM path (main.js:6309-6315) enters HELM by setting _scManual/cameraMode/bypassed inline and does NOT go through _enterFlightInternal, so it also does NOT call cameraInterp.resync; it relies on focus*() seeding scModel=camera. Since seed==camera there should be no jump, but this asymmetric entry is worth confirming.

anchorBody distance falls back to 100 when nothing is selected/closest; the clamp cancels out of position (per the contract), so this only affects zoom scale — confirm the post-exit orbit distance feels sane far out.
aspects.liveTestRecipe: E to HELM, hold W a few seconds to get far from bodies, then M to ORRERY. Capture window._cam.position and window._cam.quaternion the frame before and after the swap — assert |Δposition| < ~1e-3 and quat-dot > 0.9999 (no snap). Confirm window._cc.cameraMode==='toy_box' and window._cc._diagnostics.getSummary() shows no JUMP/ROTATION_SNAP for the transition. Reliability: run 8 HELM→ORRERY swaps at varied distances/orientations (including after Q/E roll — expect the roll-only exception) and assert position continuity every time.

aspects.name: World-origin rebasing of scModel.position + controller caches
suspectedIssues: Deep-space supercruise cruise can hit CAP_MAX=20000 u/s (SupercruiseModel.js:16); at 60Hz that is ~333 units/step, far above the 100-unit REBASE_THRESHOLD, so a rebase fires almost EVERY frame at top speed — the scene-children subtract loop runs per-frame. Functionally fine but perf/precision-under-frequent-rebase deserves a check (and the 100-unit threshold vs 333-unit step means the camera can momentarily sit ~333 units out before the next-frame rebase catches it).

One-frame lag: maybeRebase reads camera.position (from the PREVIOUS frame's applyTo) at simStep start, but scModel.position is updated and written to the camera AFTER, at 7873. The invariant relies on camera.position≈scModel.position at the check point; if any code moved the camera between frames without moving scModel (e.g. a warp/turn path), the rebase offset and scModel could diverge. Worth confirming they stay locked.

Only scModel.position is tracked; orientation/speed are frame-free (correct). But the HeadMount look and Arrival hold points are ship-relative and re-derived each frame — confirm no cached WORLD-frame supercruise vector (e.g. a pilot _holdPoint) is left untracked across a rebase (SupercruisePilot._holdPoint is world-frame and rebuilt each HOLD frame from bodyPos+_holdOffset, so likely fine, but _holdOffset is ship-relative — verify).

The WorldOrigin.js:148-150 note says the rebase assumes an UNPARENTED camera; HeadMount is deliberately not an Object3D for exactly this reason (HeadMount.js:3-7). Confirm nothing parented the camera.
aspects.liveTestRecipe: E to HELM, point at open space, hold W to CAP-out speed. Poll window._getState() (or import _debugState via window if exposed) and watch worldOrigin grow while window._cam.position stays small (|pos| < ~350). Assert window._sc.model.position stays small too (rebased) and window._sc.model.speed keeps advancing the ship (distanceTravelled via window._sc.flyFromRest as a sanity oracle). Reliability: cruise 20s, assert no visible jump/jitter (window._cc._diagnostics.getSummary().jumpCount===0 during ORRERY portions) and that a subsequent M-exit still lands no-snap. Cross-check float32 stress: near a tiny moon (radius ~1e-4) confirm capture still works after long-distance cruise (rebase kept precision).

aspects.name: ORRERY<->HELM mode-swap seams (_doModeSwap / _enterFlightInternal / cameraInterp.resync)
suspectedIssues: ENTER has no cameraInterp.resync — relies on scModel being seeded exactly to camera.position so interp curr≈prev (no lerp jump). Holds for the standard paths, but the THREE different HELM-entry sites (_enterFlightInternal, commitBurn-swap main.js:6309-6315, W/S tour-takeover 9269-9280) each set _scManual/cameraMode/bypassed slightly differently — the takeover and commit-burn paths don't call _enterFlightInternal, so any future divergence in seeding could reintroduce an entry snap. Verify all three enter snap-free.

setCameraMode(FLIGHT) inside _enterFlightInternal persists 'flight' to localStorage — this is the source of the persisted-FLIGHT landmine flagged in the legacy-FLIGHT aspect. Entering HELM permanently arms that trap until an exit re-persists 'toy_box'.
Roll snap on exit (shared with HeadMount aspect).

_doModeSwap and the E/F/M handlers share overlapping guards (warp/splash/title/star-system/mobile); a subtle guard mismatch between the key handler and the button click path could let one fire when the other refuses. mode-swap-btn label is recomputed every frame (8779-8786) which should keep it truthful.
aspects.liveTestRecipe: From ORRERY, press M → assert mode-swap-btn.textContent flips 'ORRERY'→'HELM', window._cam pose is continuous (capture before/after), window._sc.model.position===window._cam.position at entry. Press M again → 'HELM'→'ORRERY', assert no-snap (see exit aspect). Test E: from ORRERY, E engages (console '[MODE] supercruise engage', driveOn true); E again drops (driveOn false, ship settles toward rest); E again re-engages (or mass-lock blocked near a body — approach a planet, E, assert '_massLockHintFrames' path / 'reengage blocked'). Test W/S takeover during a tour: while scPilot.isActive press W → assert _scManual becomes true, pilot stops, mode-swap-btn==='HELM', and camera pose is continuous. Reliability: 10 M-swap round-trips + 5 E engage/dropout/reengage cycles, asserting label truthfulness and window._cc._diagnostics.getSummary().snapCount===0 across the ORRERY-side frames.

aspects.name: ShipCameraSystem legacy free-look + return-to-orbit (deep-sky / gyro / middle-mouse)
suspectedIssues: Two independent free-look systems coexist (ShipCameraSystem.isFreeLooking vs HeadMount/freeLook). Reachability of the legacy one in the shipping build is narrow (deep-sky/gallery/gyro); needs a live check that it hasn't silently broken during the supercruise rewire, and that the middle-mouse path never double-fires with scHead's middle-mouse peek (the peek is gated on _scManual||scPilot.isActive and cameraController.bypassed, which should keep them exclusive).
gyro path (enableGyro:833) calls enterFreeLook and is mobile-only; mobile is ORRERY-locked so no supercruise conflict, but untested here.
return-to-orbit slerp uses camera.up=(0,1,0) and a 2s delay — after deep-sky free-look, confirm the re-frame is snap-free.
aspects.liveTestRecipe: Force a deep-sky arrival (warp until system.type !== 'star-system', or inspect window._getState). Middle-mouse-drag to free-look, release — assert the camera swings then eases back to the anchor with no snap (window._cc.isFreeLooking toggles true→false; watch window._cam.quaternion continuity). Separately, in a star system during a tour, middle-mouse-drag and assert it drives scHead (window._sc.head.yaw changes) NOT window._cc.isFreeLooking (should stay false — the legacy path is suppressed). Reliability: alternate deep-sky and star-system middle-mouse looks 5× each, asserting the correct free-look owner engages each time.

aspects.name: CameraChoreographer — authored camera-axis dispatch (ESTABLISHING/linger/pan-ahead)
suspectedIssues: DEAD-WEIGHT/DORMANT: CameraChoreographer's only live driver (FlythroughCamera) is retired and gated behind SHIPS_ENABLED=false (main.js:152). Its linger/pan-ahead framing does not run for supercruise tours — the tour's camera look is entirely scModel.orientation via scHead. So the 'linger on receding subject / pan-ahead' cinematic beats it implements are NOT what the live screensaver does; that framing now lives (if anywhere) in SupercruisePilot HOLD + the shake choreographer. Risk of stale mental model: reviewers may think this authors the tour camera.

It is still constructed, exposed on window._cameraChoreographer/_cc-adjacent debug hooks (main.js:916, 958-962), and its caches are rebase-tracked every frame — non-zero maintenance cost for a dormant module.

If SHIPS_ENABLED is ever flipped true (ENRICHED reactivation), this path resurrects with the old legacy framing — would need re-validation against the supercruise camera conventions (it writes look targets for camera.lookAt, not the scHead pose).
aspects.liveTestRecipe: Confirm dormancy: during a normal warp→tour, poll window._cameraChoreographer.currentMode and window._cameraChoreographer.framingState — assert framingState never advances past its idle/TRACKING default and that window._flythrough.active stays false throughout (i.e. the choreographer never ticks). Assert the tour camera look is driven by window._sc.model.orientation (compare camera forward to scModel.nose()) not by window._cameraChoreographer.currentLookAtTarget. Reliability: watch across 3 full tour+auto-warp cycles; assert flythrough.active===false every frame. (To exercise the module at all would require SHIPS_ENABLED=true + a ship target — out of scope for the shipping build.)

aspects.name: trySelect() priority cascade (minimap → in-system body → orbit line → deep-sky particle → background star)
suspectedIssues: Ordering hazard in HELM hands-on: the minimap-consume block (9370-9409) runs BEFORE the center-override (9417). In HELM the OS cursor is hidden and the mouse position is the flight stick, so if the invisible stick happens to sit over the minimap circle at click time (minimap toggled on via C), the click is swallowed by systemMap.hitTest instead of selecting the center-reticle body — center-select silently fails.

Step 1b only builds targets for orbitHit.info.type 'planet'/'moon' (9441-9448); a 'star' orbit-line hit (binary star orbit rings) yields target=null and the click falls through to deep-sky/star selection.

Step 2 particle branch returns without enforcing the single-selection invariant that step 3 enforces (does not deselect _selectedTarget, does not clear warpTarget metadata) — see the dedicated deep-sky aspect.
aspects.liveTestRecipe: Enter Sol: window._lab.enterSol(). ORRERY: click a planet's screen center → window._getReticleState().selected shows that planet. Click near the star → star selected (not a bg star). Toggle minimap (press C) then click just outside the minimap circle over empty sky → window._warpTarget.direction becomes non-null (bg-star pick); click INSIDE the circle → selection unchanged (consumed). HELM regression: press M to swap to HELM (confirm document.getElementById('mode-swap-btn').textContent==='HELM'), turn minimap ON (C), then dispatch a real mousedown+mouseup at coords OVER the minimap region while nose is on a planet → confirm the planet is NOT selected (reproduces the swallow); repeat with minimap OFF → planet selected. Assert reproducibility over 5 clicks each.

aspects.name: hitTestBodies() — forgiving screen-space body pick with adaptive threshold + kind tie-break
suspectedIssues: Rebuilds a fresh _makeTarget object for EVERY body on EVERY call, and the call runs once per frame for hover (8500) plus once per mousemove (9734) plus per click — O(bodies) allocation each frame; fine for small systems but a GC/perf smell in dense systems.
Uses camera.fov directly for pixelRadius; if a transient FOV change (warp/effects) is in flight the threshold could momentarily mis-size, though selection is guarded off during warp.
Ships rank 0 (below moons) so a ship exactly overlapping a moon is never selectable while both project to the same pixel — intended, but means some ships are unclickable when parked at a body.
aspects.liveTestRecipe: window._lab.enterSol(). Compute a planet's screen coords from window._scene/window._cam projection (or just probe): call window._hitTestBodies(cx,cy) at the planet's screen center → returns {kind:'planet',...}. Nudge 20px off → still hits (adaptive+12 margin). Move 200px off → null. Overlap test: fly/orbit until Earth's moon sits on Earth's disk, window._hitTestBodies at the shared pixel → kind==='planet' (tie-break). Scanner: window._lab.setShipScannerMode(true) with ships present → window._hitTestBodies over a ship returns kind==='ship'.

aspects.name: hitTestOrbits() — click an orbit line to select its body
suspectedIssues: Per-vertex screen projection of every orbit line every call is O(totalOrbitVertices); combined with the per-mousemove hover call this is the heaviest selection-path cost in dense systems.
trySelect uses threshold 6px but hover highlight uses 8px — a line can highlight on hover yet not select on click in the 6-8px band (feels unresponsive).
info.type 'star' (binary star orbit rings, if present in _orbitLineTargets) is not mapped to a target in trySelect (9441-9448) → clicking a star's orbit ring does nothing / falls through.

In HELM hands-on the center-override means orbit-line clicks are effectively unreachable (aim is forced to center), so this is ORRERY/free-look-only in practice — not wrong, but undocumented at the call site.
aspects.liveTestRecipe: window._lab.enterSol() in ORRERY, ensure orbits visible (press O if needed; window.__ or check system.orbitLines[].mesh.visible). Move cursor onto a planet's orbit ellipse (away from the planet dot): the line should brighten to green + cursor 'pointer'. Click on the line → window._getReticleState().selected == that planet. Repeat at a point 5px from the line (in the 6-8px gap) → hover may highlight but click may miss; note the discrepancy. Try a moon orbit ring → moon selected.

aspects.name: selectTarget() soft-select + _selectedTarget state + camera aim + BodyInfo
suspectedIssues: The camera re-center is gated on !cameraController.bypassed (6193); in HELM/autopilot bypassed is true, so selecting a body does NOT re-aim the view there — selection is purely reticle+state in flight, which is intended but means 'select' has visibly different feel across modes.

_isSameTarget returns false for ships (476-483), so a selected ship never suppresses its own hover reticle (double bracket draw) and can never satisfy aimOnTarget (no contextual ETA) — inconsistent with celestial bodies.

BodyInfo is shown on every selectTarget, but the minimap/autopilot jump path and commit path set _selectedTarget directly (2749, 6848) bypassing selectTarget — so BodyInfo/sound can be skipped on those selection routes (inconsistent side-effects for 'a selection').
aspects.liveTestRecipe: window._lab.enterSol(). ORRERY: window._lab.selectBody('planet',2) → window._lab.selectedTarget() returns planet 2; BURN button (#commit-burn-btn) display=='block'; window._getReticleState().selected.kind==='planet'; confirm the god's-eye view eased-recenters on the planet. window._lab.selectBody('star',0) → warpTarget cleared (window._warpTarget.direction===null) proving single-selection. window._lab.deselectBody() → selected null, button hidden. In HELM (M): window._lab.selectBody('planet',3) → selected set, button stays hidden (see BURN-button aspect), and confirm _sc.controls / _flightMode re-armed (window._sc.controls host flightMode).

aspects.name: HELM center-reticle click-select (cursor hidden → click selects what the nose points at)
suspectedIssues: Empty-space fallthrough: if the nose is NOT on a body, the center cascade continues to deep-sky particle then trySelectWarpTarget(center ray) — so a HELM select-click on empty sky silently selects a BACKGROUND STAR as a warp target (green blink brackets appear mid-flight). Mode-inappropriate surprise; nothing gates star-warp selection out of HELM hands-on.
Minimap swallow (see cascade aspect): the minimap-consume block runs on the RAW (invisible-stick) coords before the center override, so an on-minimap stick position defeats center-select.

There is no visible commit affordance for a HELM selection (BURN button suppressed while _scManual) — the player must know to press Space; the center-select gives a reticle but no on-screen 'commit' hint.

isDrag gate is disabled for the WHOLE hands-on regime; any stray large mouse motion between down/up still selects at center — generally fine, but means you cannot 'cancel' a click by dragging in HELM.
aspects.liveTestRecipe: window._lab.enterSol(); press M to HELM (mode-swap-btn text 'HELM'); confirm F not toggled (cursor hidden: canvas.style.cursor==='none'). Fly (W to throttle up, steer with mouse) so a planet crosses screen center → window._getReticleState().hover shows that planet (dim bracket). Dispatch mousedown+mouseup anywhere → window._lab.selectedTarget() == that planet (NOT a star). Then point the nose at empty sky and click → observe window._warpTarget.direction becomes non-null (the empty-space-selects-a-star bug). Repeat select-on-body 5× to confirm reliability. Minimap case as in the cascade recipe.

aspects.name: COMMIT BURN button + commitBurn() (with ORRERY→HELM auto-swap for celestial targets)
suspectedIssues: Button is fully suppressed in HELM (_scManual in the burning mask, 6417) — a HELM selection has NO visible commit button; commit is Space-only. Intended per design but means the labelled affordance exists in one mode only.

commitBurn's ORRERY→HELM swap bypasses _enterFlightInternal (comment 6295-6314) and hand-rolls the regime flip (setScManual+setCameraMode+bypassed+_applyPointerHud); any future step added to _enterFlightInternal won't run on this path (drift risk).

Ship burns deliberately DON'T swap to HELM (commitBurnSwapsToHelm excludes ship) and stay on quarantined navSubsystem — so a ship BURN behaves differently (ORRERY-only motion) than a planet BURN; if a ship is selected and _scManual were somehow true the burn path diverges.

The button label uppercases _selectedTarget.name || 'TARGET'; deep-sky/particle warp targets never set _selectedTarget so no button — consistent, but the 'TARGET' fallback is only reachable for a nameless body.
aspects.liveTestRecipe: window._lab.enterSol() in ORRERY. window._lab.selectBody('planet',2): assert #commit-burn-btn display 'block' and textContent startsWith 'BURN → '. Click it (or window._lab.commitBurnNow()): assert window._sc.pilot.isActive===true, mode-swap-btn text flips to 'HELM' (auto-swap), _flightMode ASSIST (window._sc.controls host flightMode() === 'assist'), button hidden. Now inject a W keydown or mouse deflection → assert scPilot.stop fires (window._sc.pilot.isActive false, manual takeover). Ship case: window._lab.setShipScannerMode(true); window._lab.selectShip(0); commitBurnNow() → assert mode-swap-btn STAYS 'ORRERY' (no swap) and navSubsystem drives (window._sc.pilot.isActive false).

aspects.name: commitSelection() — universal Space commit (3-stage portal-preview warp OR in-system burn)
suspectedIssues: Two divergent warp-commit mechanisms coexist: desktop Space uses the 3-stage portal preview (commitSelection); autopilot/deep-sky/touch/mobile use beginWarpTurn (camera slerp then warpEffect.start at 7334-7342). Mobile and touch users therefore never get the preview/align stages — inconsistent commit UX and two code paths to keep in sync.

_portalLabState is a persistent module state ('survives across warps'); if a warp is aborted or a system swap interrupts mid-'preview'/'aligning', the next Space could land in an unexpected stage. onComplete resets to 'idle' but non-warp interruptions may not.
commitSelection returns early (no-op) if warpTarget.turning — but the turning path is the beginWarpTurn flow; if both a warpTarget.direction and a turning state ever coexist Space is swallowed.
A3 (double-click star commits warp) was specced to be an ADDITIONAL commit path to Space but is not implemented (see dedicated aspect) — so Space is the only manual warp commit.
aspects.liveTestRecipe: window._lab.enterSol(). Select a bg star: window._autoSelectWarpTarget() (sets window._warpTarget.direction). Press Space (or window._commitSelection()) three times, checking window._getState().labState after each: 'preview' → 'aligning' → warp fires (window._getState().warp===true). Body-burn path: window._lab.selectBody('planet',2); window._commitSelection() → returns true, scPilot.isActive true, no warp. No-op: window._lab.deselectBody(); window._warpTarget.direction=null; window._commitSelection() → returns false, nothing changes. Mobile-divergence check: on a touch build, double-tap → confirm warp starts via warpTarget.turning (window._warpTarget.turning true) NOT via labState progression.

aspects.name: In-system targeting brackets (dim hover / bright selected / ghost lock-in) + per-frame aim hover + occlusion
suspectedIssues: hitTestBodies now runs every frame (8500) as the hover source AND still runs on every mousemove (9734) for cursor feedback — double hit-testing per input frame (perf smell, acknowledged as 'no costlier' in spec but the mousemove one is now redundant for hover).

In HELM free-look with LMB held (look-drag) the cursor still moves and _mouseX/_mouseY still update (9725 unconditional), so the hover follows the cursor during a look-drag — the spec mode-matrix says this row should be 'frozen at last aim'. Minor divergence from the documented contract.
Ship hover vs selected-ship: _isSameTarget returns false for ships, so a selected ship still gets a dim hover bracket drawn under its bright ship bracket (double draw).
Occlusion is analytic ray/sphere against _occluders rebuilt each frame; a body only partially occluding (edge grazing) can pop the reticle on/off as positions jitter.
aspects.liveTestRecipe: window._lab.enterSol(). ORRERY: move cursor over a planet → window._getReticleState().hover == that planet; window._reticle.getLastFrameState() shows a 'ghost'/'target' draw tightening over ~400ms. window._lab.selectBody('planet',2) → hover on the same body now null (suppression), selected bright. HELM (M, cursor hidden): with no mouse motion, throttle up and steer so a body crosses center → window._getReticleState().hover populates purely from flying (proves center-aim). Occlusion: position camera so planet B is directly behind planet A along the ray → assert B's reticle drops from window._reticle.getLastFrameState(). Regression: in HELM free-look (F), hold LMB and drag → check whether hover freezes (spec) or follows cursor (current).

aspects.name: Contextual ETA (M:SS drop counter gated on aim-on-destination)
suspectedIssues: aimOnTarget can never be true for a ship destination (_isSameTarget returns false for ships) and _resolveSelectedBody excludes ships, so the ETA/drop marker never tracks a ship burn — a ship transit shows no ETA even though focusShip is a real leg.

targetPos falls back to scControls.target?.mesh?.position when nothing is _selectedTarget (autopilot tour), but _aimOnTarget requires _selectedTarget — so during the system-picked tour (no _selectedTarget) the ETA counter never shows even when the nose is on the tour destination (only player-picked legs get contextual ETA).
ETA = distance/speed is a straight-line instantaneous estimate ignoring the gravity-well speed cap and decel curve, so it will read optimistically low as you approach and the cap collapses.
aspects.liveTestRecipe: window._lab.enterSol(); commit a burn to a planet (window._lab.selectBody('planet',2); window._lab.commitBurnNow()). While flying, aim the nose/cursor ONTO the destination planet → the SupercruiseHud shows an M:SS ETA below the body. Steer the nose AWAY → ETA line disappears entirely (drop label if any stays). Confirm via window._sc.hud state or a screenshot. Tour case: window._lab.beginAutopilotTour() with no _selectedTarget → confirm NO ETA counter appears even when the tour target crosses center (documents the tour gap). Ship case: selectShip+commitBurnNow → confirm ETA never appears.

aspects.name: Warp-target selection via background star / galactic feature / external galaxy + green blink brackets + single-selection invariant
suspectedIssues: The resolved star index/data is snapshotted at pick time because starfield regeneration invalidates the index (comment 9492) — correct, but if the sky regenerates between pick and commit the stored navStarData is the only anchor; any bug there silently warps to a direction-generated system instead of the picked star.

In HELM hands-on this is the unintended fallthrough target for an empty-space click (see HELM select aspect) — the single-selection deselect here will also silently drop a HELM body selection when the player only meant to click.

Brackets are a shader overlay (setTargetUniforms) entirely separate from the TargetingReticle DOM/canvas brackets — two independent 'bracket' systems with different look/occlusion logic; easy to confuse when auditing.
aspects.liveTestRecipe: window._lab.enterSol(). Aim at empty sky and click (ORRERY) → window._warpTarget.direction non-null, .name populated, green brackets blink on screen; if a body was selected first, window._lab.selectedTarget() returns null after (single-selection). Feature/galaxy routing: repeatedly window._autoSelectWarpTarget() and read window._warpTarget.destType until you get 'feature:*' or 'external-galaxy' — confirm .name/.featureData/.galaxyData set. Commit: Space ×3 (3-stage) → warp fires; after emergence window._getState().warp false and a new system loaded. Reliability: loop {autoSelectWarpTarget; commitSelection×3; wait for emergence} 5× asserting each completes.

aspects.name: Deep-sky particle warp-target selection (galaxy/globular destinations)
suspectedIssues: Does NOT enforce the single-selection invariant: unlike trySelectWarpTarget (9485) and _setWarpTargetFromNavStar (2823), it neither deselects a live _selectedTarget nor calls _clearWarpTargetSelection — so a stale _selectedTarget AND warpTarget.direction can be set simultaneously (commitSelection prefers direction, but the reticle/BURN state is inconsistent).

Leaves warpTarget.name / destType / navStarData / featureData / galaxyData / starIndex at their PREVIOUS values — if a feature/galaxy was picked earlier, a subsequent particle pick inherits that stale destType, so onPrepareSystem may route the warp to the wrong destination category or the portal seed uses a stale/`dest-${seedCounter}` name.
No 'warpTarget' sound and no bodyInfo.showWarpTarget label on the particle path (unlike star selection) — the pick is silent/unlabelled.
Reachability/behavior depends entirely on system.destination.findNearestParticle existing; unclear which destination systems expose it — status of the actual in-game path is unverified.
aspects.liveTestRecipe: Reach a deep-sky destination system (warp toward a galaxy/globular feature until window._lab.systemInfo().destinationName is set / system.type !== 'star-system'). First select nothing; click a visible cluster particle → window._warpTarget.direction set, and inspect window._warpTarget.name/destType — confirm whether they are stale from the prior selection (bug) or cleared. Then: window._lab.selectBody(...) is likely unavailable (no planets); instead set warpTarget via a prior star pick, deselect, then particle-pick and check _selectedTarget is still null. Commit Space×3 and verify the emergent system matches the particle direction (not a stale feature). If findNearestParticle is absent, mark path unreachable.

aspects.name: autoSelectWarpTarget() — screensaver auto-pick warp target
suspectedIssues: Correctly resets destType/featureData/galaxyData (9548-9550) but does NOT deselect a live _selectedTarget or clear warpTarget.name from a prior pick before overwriting — minor since it overwrites name in all branches, but if getRandomVisibleStar returns null it early-returns leaving whatever was there (beginWarpTurn then aborts, 9606-9610).

getRandomVisibleStar depends on the forward hemisphere having a visible star; in a sparse inter-arm gap it could return null and the auto-warp aborts (logged warning at 9608) — the screensaver could stall on a starless view.
aspects.liveTestRecipe: window._lab.enterSol(). window._autoSelectWarpTarget() → window._warpTarget.direction non-null, .name set, .destType null|'feature:*'|'external-galaxy'. Confirm brackets blink on screen. Screensaver reliability loop: window._lab.stopAutopilot() off; let idle → autopilot tour → auto-warp, OR script {window._autoSelectWarpTarget(); window._beginWarpTurn()} and wait for window._getState().warp then emergence; repeat 5-10× asserting each completes and no '[WARP] No star found' warning. Starless case: rotate camera to a sparse gap (window._cam), call _autoSelectWarpTarget(), check for null/abort.

aspects.name: A3 — second click on an already-selected star commits the warp
suspectedIssues: Spec Thread A A3 (and A2) were approved 'ready to implement' but only Thread B (roll+remap) and A1 (orbit-default-by-mode) landed — A2/A3 are missing, so the only manual warp commit remains Space (double-click-to-warp does not exist).

AC3's 'single click never warps' is trivially satisfied only because there IS no click-warp at all; the intended second-click affordance is absent, so the spec's stated UX (confirm-by-second-click) is unmet.

Because A2 is also missing, clicking a planet on the minimap still fires a FULL supercruise burn (focusPlanet→flyTo) rather than the '~0.3s eased view move' the spec describes — a behavioral mismatch, not just a missing feature.
aspects.liveTestRecipe: window._lab.enterSol() in ORRERY. Click a background star → window._warpTarget.direction set (selected+blink). Click the EXACT same star again → EXPECTED per spec: warp begins (window._getState().warp or window._warpTarget.turning true). ACTUAL (predicted): still just re-selected, no warp. Confirm no warp fires on the second click, demonstrating the gap. Cross-check A2: click a planet on the minimap → observe a full burn (window._sc.pilot.isActive true) rather than a ~0.3s camera ease, confirming A2 also unimplemented.

aspects.name: Minimap click-to-select / jump (systemMap.hitTest routing)
suspectedIssues: Manual-mode minimap planet click calls focusPlanet → a FULL supercruise ASSIST burn (flyTo linger:Infinity), not the spec-A2 '~0.3s eased view move' — the minimap 'select' silently launches a transit (and, since focusPlanet runs at !_scManual, it does NOT auto-swap to HELM here because it goes through focusPlanet directly, not commitBurn — so the player is left flying an ASSIST leg while still labelled ORRERY).

aspects.name: ShipControls.flyTo — the single pilot-leg dispatch door
suspectedIssues: In-game callers must remember selfStep:false; the DEFAULT is selfStep:true (headless self-step). A future caller that forgets it would spin flyTo's internal 100000-step loop synchronously on the main thread and desync the live sim. No runtime guard enforces the live convention.

flyTo overwrites this._arrival each call with no cancel of a prior in-flight Arrival; back-to-back legs (rapid Tab/number jumps) rely on beginLeg resetting pilot phase rather than the Arrival being cleanly retired.

During the tour, log window._sc.pilot.phase each second — assert it cycles ALIGN→CRUISE→HOLD and that window._sc.pilot._target.mesh changes at each stop. Press Tab to force-advance and confirm _target flips and phase resets to ALIGN. aspects.name: ShipControls.step — safe pilot-before-model ordering + arrival poll
suspectedIssues: The Arrival is polled ONLY when pilot.isActive; a manual-stick leg (scActive via _scManual, pilot idle) never polls, which is correct but means any Arrival left set from a cancelled pilot leg is never resolved/rejected until the next flyTo replaces it (minor leak of a resolved-never Arrival).

Ordering safety depends on callers never invoking model.update elsewhere; the drive-forced-drop block (main.js:7841-7846) mutates model state (setDrive/setThrottle) BEFORE step() the same tick — correct, but it is an out-of-surface write to the model the door doesn't mediate.
aspects.liveTestRecipe: In HELM tour, set window._sc.pilot to active and confirm window._sc.controls.step is the only per-frame stepper: null out cameraController by watching window._cam pose only moves via scHead.applyTo. Measure: sample window._sc.model.position each frame during a CRUISE leg — position delta direction should equal window._sc.model.nose() (translation only along nose). Reliability: over a full tour, assert position is monotonic toward each target during CRUISE and frozen (lerp-settled) during HOLD.

aspects.name: ShipControls.engage / disengage vs host _enter/_exitFlightInternal (door asymmetry)
suspectedIssues: ShipControls.disengage() is DEAD CODE in the live game — the 'single door' for exit is really the host fn _exitFlightInternal, reached by multiple call sites, not the surface method. The surface's engage/disengage are near-vestigial wrappers (engage used once).

The claimed symmetry ('both go through this object') holds for flyTo/step/select/steer but NOT for enter/exit: the true door is _enterFlightInternal/_exitFlightInternal at the host layer. A reader trusting ShipControls as the choke point would miss the 4+ direct-to-internal entry paths.

Because entries are scattered (some via scControls.engage→enterFlight, some inline setScManual(true)+setCameraMode), the invariants enterFlight enforces (freeLook.exit, _applyPointerHud, _enterFlightMode) are re-implemented ad hoc at the inline sites (e.g. commit-burn swap main.js:6310-6313 hand-rolls regime flip + _applyPointerHud without _enterFlightMode).

deselect is also reached from focusPlanet(-1) flows indirectly; the single-selection invariant relies on _clearWarpTargetSelection being called in selectTarget only, not deselect — a warp pick set after a deselect is not re-cleared.

aspects.name: ShipControls.steer — virtual-joystick single door + casing fix + deflection sync
suspectedIssues: The mousemove handler computes shapeStick TWICE per move — once inline for the _deflected gate (main.js:9687) and again inside scControls.steer (main.js:9700). Correct only because both read the same _scStickTuning with identical lowercased opts; any future divergence (one uppercase) silently re-introduces the ignored-tuning bug the casing fix closed.
Roll (Q/E) is written to model.turnInput.roll directly in the WASD block (main.js:8139), NOT through the steer door — so the 'single door' covers yaw/pitch only; roll bypasses ShipControls entirely.

Steering reads ABSOLUTE canvas-center offset (not the shaped value clamp), so window rAF throttle (~1fps on unfocused tab) will freeze deflection updates and make the joystick appear dead in a background tab.

Move mouse to a corner: read window._sc.model.turnInput (yaw/pitch should be non-zero, opposite sign to _scDeflection) and confirm the HUD deflection dot tracks. aspects.name: _enterFlightInternal — the real HELM-entry door
suspectedIssues: It reads Settings flightControlType and calls _enterFlightMode — so ANY entry (including M-swap and R-engage) with Settings set to Assist/Align AND a body selected will START A PILOT LEG on entry. For M-swap the mode-restructure spec says 'swap stations only, drive untouched' — but this can silently begin an Assist fly-to, which is more than a station swap. Default flightControlType='manual' hides this; a non-default Settings value changes M's behavior.

It NEVER touches scModel.setDrive. Combined with SupercruiseModel._driveOn defaulting to TRUE (SupercruiseModel.js:47), an entry via this fn with drive still at default-on immediately cruises to MIN_CRUISE (2.0 u/s) on the next tick (see warp HELM cold-open aspect).

It copies camera.quaternion into model.orientation; if entered while the camera carries a HeadMount look offset, that offset is baked into ship heading. Guarded in practice because prior exit zeroes scHead (main.js:8728-8731) and entry clears freeLook, but no assertion that scHead.yaw/pitch are 0 at copy time.
aspects.liveTestRecipe: Set Settings flightControlType to 'assist', select a planet in ORRERY, then press M (swap to HELM): assert window._sc.pilot.isActive becomes TRUE (a leg started) — this reveals M starting an Assist leg. Reset to 'manual' and repeat: assert pilot stays idle. Separately: from ORRERY press R (engage): read window._sc.model.orientation vs window._cam quaternion — assert they match the pre-entry camera pose (no snap) and window._sc.model.throttle===0.

aspects.name: _exitFlightInternal — the no-snap HELM→ORRERY exit door
suspectedIssues: The no-snap invariant depends on adoptCurrentPose/cameraInterp.resync matching flightExitAnchor's assumed reconstruction math; if ShipCameraSystem's _applyOrbit formula ever changes, the anchor silently stops cancelling and the 2026-06-25 body-center re-anchor snap returns (the spec's explicit regression risk). No live guard beyond the headless camera test.

Under floating-origin drift the anchor uses camera.position and the body mesh only for the pivot SCALE (d), so it should be drift-safe — but if worldOrigin was rebased on the SAME frame as exit, findClosestBody()/selected mesh could be on a stale origin, skewing d (only the pivot scale, not pos, per the contract).
It does NOT setDrive(false); leaving HELM while the drive was ON means re-entering (M back) resumes with drive ON (default), which is arguably intended but not stated.
aspects.liveTestRecipe: In HELM, drift the world origin (fly a long CRUISE leg), then read window._cam.position + quaternion, press M (HELM→ORRERY), immediately re-read: assert dPos < 1e-4 scene units and quatDot(before,after) ≈ 1.0 (no snap). Confirm document.getElementById('mode-swap-btn').textContent flips HELM→ORRERY. Reliability: 8 M-swap round-trips (HELM→ORRERY→HELM) at increasing drift, asserting no cumulative camera drift and focusIndex===-1 after each HELM→ORRERY.

aspects.name: _doModeSwap — M key / HUD button / Options peer-mode swap
suspectedIssues: modeSwapAction promises lightDrive:false, but ORRERY→HELM calls _enterFlightInternal() which does NOT touch drive AND leaves _driveOn at its prior/default value — if default TRUE, the swap-to-HELM silently starts cruising at MIN_CRUISE, i.e. the swap DOES effectively 'light' motion even though it never calls setDrive. 'Drive untouched' ≠ 'drive off'.

_enterFlightInternal() (no type) reads Settings flightControlType and can start an Assist/Align leg on M-swap-to-HELM when a body is selected — contradicting the 'swap stations only' framing (see _enterFlightInternal aspect).

The console log prints target from swap (pre-computed) but the guards can no-op silently (mobile/warp/non-star-system) with no user feedback beyond a console line; the HUD button is hidden in those cases (main.js:8782), so at least the button can't offer a refused swap — but the M KEY can be pressed and no-op quietly.
aspects.liveTestRecipe: From ORRERY (mode-swap-btn text 'ORRERY'), press M: assert text flips to 'HELM', _scManual true, and — critically — read window._sc.model.driveOn and speed over 2s to see whether the ship begins moving (drive default-on cruise). Click the HUD button and the Options item and confirm each performs the identical swap (text toggles). Guard test: start a warp (window._beginWarpTurn()) then spam M — assert no mode change (button hidden, _scManual unchanged). Reliability: 10 M presses alternating directions; assert button text and _scManual stay in lockstep every press.

aspects.name: BLACK ORRERY/HELM boot picker (_pickBootMode + bootModeAction)
suspectedIssues: LEAK on deep-sky first warp: warpRevealSystem's distant-deep-sky branch RETURNS at main.js:6001 BEFORE the _pendingBootMode consume/reset at main.js:6018-6019. autoSelectWarpTarget can (rarely) pick an external galaxy / galactic feature (main.js:9538-9540 'rarely an external galaxy'), so a HELM pick whose first warp lands on deep sky is NOT consumed and leaks into the NEXT star-system arrival — the player watches an ORRERY galaxy, then the following star warp unexpectedly boots into HELM.

The D-hold debug skip (main.js:2496-2516) spawns Sol via _debugEnterKnownSystem, which bypasses warpRevealSystem entirely — a HELM pick then D-skip never consumes _pendingBootMode; it leaks to the first real warp and 'helm' silently persists.

_pickBootMode only fires while splashActive; if the intro is somehow re-entered the guard prevents a second pick, but there is no reset of _pendingBootMode on a full reload-less restart (not reachable in normal play).

To force the deep-sky leak: before the auto-warp, set the warp target to a galaxy (or repeatedly reload until autoSelectWarpTarget picks one — check window._warpTarget.destType==='external-galaxy'), let it warp; after arrival assert you're in ORRERY deep-sky free-look, then read _pendingBootMode still === 'helm' (leaked). Warp again to a star and assert it (wrongly) boots HELM. Normal path: HELM pick → star arrival → assert document.getElementById('mode-swap-btn').textContent==='HELM' and _scManual===true; ORRERY pick → assert autopilot tour runs (window._sc.pilot.isActive) and text 'ORRERY'.

aspects.name: warpRevealSystem boot-mode consumption + HELM cold-open drive state
suspectedIssues: 'Drive untouched' cold-open cruises: SupercruiseModel._driveOn defaults TRUE (SupercruiseModel.js:47) and neither _seedScPoseFromCameraIfIdle nor _enterFlightInternal calls setDrive. With drive ON + throttle 0, model.update targets clamp(0, floorEff, cap) = MIN_CRUISE (2.0 u/s) — so the HELM cold-open immediately accelerates forward along the warp-exit nose (toward the star). Whether that is the intended 'arrival glide' or an unexpected auto-cruise is unverified; the spec language ('drive untouched') does not describe motion-on-boot.

_seedScPoseFromCameraIfIdle() at main.js:6023 is redundant — _enterFlightInternal re-seeds the model from the camera two lines later (main.js:8656-8659). Harmless but signals the seam wasn't fully reconciled.

The HELM boot skips the ORRERY orbit-line default (_syncOrbitsToMode at main.js:6033 is after the early return), which is correct for HELM (orbits off) but means orbit visibility is set only via setScManual→_syncOrbitsToMode inside _enterFlightInternal — relies on that chain firing.

IMMEDIATELY on arrival poll window._sc.model.{driveOn,speed,throttle} every 250ms for 4s: driveOn is expected true (default), throttle 0 — assert whether speed climbs toward 2.0 (confirms auto-cruise cold-open) or stays 0. Confirm window._sc.pilot.isActive===false (no tour leg) and _scManual===true. Reliability: 3 HELM cold-opens (reload each), asserting identical drive/speed behavior each time and that the mode-swap button reads HELM.

aspects.name: setScManual — regime flag + side-effect fan-out
suspectedIssues: Cursor-by-mode (_applyPointerHud) is NOT fanned out from setScManual — it is applied SEPARATELY at each call site (enter/exit/swap/commit/takeover). So a future path that flips _scManual without also calling _applyPointerHud would desync the cursor/reticle from the regime (the tour W/S takeover explicitly adds it at main.js:9278 precisely because setScManual doesn't).

_syncOrbitsToMode early-returns if _orbitsUserOverride (main.js:6686) — once the player presses O, orbit visibility no longer follows the regime, which is intended but means a later 'orbits should be off in HELM' expectation silently won't hold after any manual O toggle.

aspects.name: commit-burn ORRERY→HELM auto-swap (select-and-jump Assist leg)
suspectedIssues: The auto-swap flips regime INLINE (setScManual+setCameraMode+bypassed) and never calls _enterFlightInternal, so it skips _enterFlightMode AND skips clearing a stray freeLook.latch — a commit from ORRERY is fine (no HELM free-look), but the code path diverges from the canonical enter door (invariants hand-rolled).

Neither commitBurn nor focus*→flyTo calls scModel.setDrive(true). The SupercruisePilot issues throttle (CRUISE_THROTTLE 0.75) but the SPEED depends on model.driveOn: if the player had previously DROPPED OUT (drive OFF) in HELM and then commits/reselects, the Assist leg runs in the sublight regime (cap 0.002 u/s) and effectively never reaches the target — the pilot ALIGN/CRUISE logic assumes supercruise speeds. commitBurnSwapsToHelm only sets regime, not drive; from ORRERY drive is default-on so it usually works, but an in-HELM reselect-while-dropped path (selectTarget→_engageAssist, main.js:6208) has no drive guard at all.

Assert _scManual flips true, mode-swap button 'HELM', window._sc.pilot.isActive true, _flightMode==='assist', and window._sc.model.driveOn true (default) so speed rises. Mid-burn, inject W (throttle) or a stick move: assert window._sc.pilot.isActive goes false and _flightMode resets to 'manual' (takeover). Drive-OFF edge: in HELM press R to drop out (driveOn false), select a far planet, Space: assert whether the Assist leg crawls (speed stuck ~0.002) — confirms the missing setDrive(true) on Assist. Reliability: 5 ORRERY select+Space cycles to distinct bodies, asserting each reaches HOLD and each is cancellable by W.

completenessCritic:
Completeness critique of the flight-systems audit. Every point grounded in a file/line I verified this session.

## (a) Flight aspects present in code/docs but NOT covered by any cluster

1. **The SupercruiseHud render surface itself is unaudited.** `src/ui/SupercruiseHud.js` is a whole flight-instrument layer — numeric speed + bidirectional SUBLIGHT/forward log-speed bar (lines 102–120), bidirectional throttle bar with commanded pin (136–160), drop-here tick + SAFE TO DROP/SLOW DOWN labels (129–216), the MODE readout (223–229), the free-look reticle-hide gate `showReticle` (168–176). The audit only ever touches this file for `massLockHint` and `etaVisible`. No aspect verifies the speed/throttle/drop-window readouts render correctly or track the model. It is its own canvas at `zIndex:51` (line 25) separate from the WebGL and TargetingReticle canvases — a third overlay system.

2. **DPR / multi-monitor / resize handling for the flight HUD.** `SupercruiseHud._resize()` recomputes DPR only on the `resize` event (line 32) and clamps `devicePixelRatio` to `min(2, …)` (line 36). Moving the window between a 1× and a 2× monitor does not reliably fire `resize`, so the HUD (and the deflection dot radius `min(innerWidth,innerHeight)*0.25`, line 172) can render at the wrong scale mid-flight. No cluster examines resolution/DPR robustness for any flight overlay.

3. **The fixed-timestep loop + background-throttle is a flight-reliability surface, not just a test caveat.** `createAccumulator({ stepMs: 1000/60, maxStepMs: 100 })` (main.js:6795) driven by `bindToRAF` (8616). The whole sim — model step, pilot, rebasing, tour timers — is rAF-gated and clamped to ≤6 substeps/wake. The audit treats "keep the window focused, rAF throttles to ~1fps" as a *measurement caveat* in ~20 recipes, but never as a **finding**: the screensaver's intended runtime (unattended, possibly a background/secondary monitor) is exactly the state where the sim throttles/pauses. See (c) below.

4. **Number-key (1–9) and Tab body-focus in *non-autopilot* ORRERY are un-covered entry points to the uncancellable ORRERY burn.** Keydown 9346–9351 routes `1`–`9` → `focusPlanet(idx)` and 9332–9341 routes Tab/Shift-Tab → `focusPlanet` cycle. `focusPlanet` (6504), `focusStar` (6566), `focusMoon` (6616) all set `cameraController.bypassed=true` + `scControls.flyTo({linger:Infinity})` + `_flightMode=playerBurnMode()` but **never `setScManual(true)` and never swap to HELM**. The audit attributes the "uncancellable ORRERY burn" only to *minimap clicks* (A2 / minimap aspects); the keyboard is an equal, unmentioned trigger.

5. **Continuous flight audio does not exist.** `SoundEngine.play()` (SoundEngine.js:107) fires discrete one-shot samples only; there is no throttle/speed-sonified engine bed (grep of main.js `sfx.play` shows only `select`/`autopilotOn/Off`/`warpCharge/Enter/Exit`/`warpTarget`/`warpLockOn`). PLAYER_EXPERIENCE.md:61 marks all SFX as placeholders, so this is intended-placeholder, not a defect — but "feels like Elite supercruise" has zero audio dimension today and no cluster notes it.

6. **Stick tuning (deadzone/expo) is runtime-only, never persisted.** `Settings.js` DEFAULTS (10–63) has `flightControlType`, `fov`, `zoomSensitivity`, `autoRotateSpeed`, but **no** stick deadzone/expo/sensitivity. `_scStickTuning` (referenced by the steer aspects) lives only on `window._sc.stickTuning`, so any UAT-tuned feel is lost on reload. The audit's steer aspects never note this asymmetry.

7. **`celestialTimeMultiplier` (Settings.js:37, applied main.js:6956 → 7026/7048) is a flight input no cluster models.** It can be set anywhere from **−10000× to +10000×** (Settings.js:33–37). Every tour/assist leg's steering is pure pursuit reading the *live* body each frame (`steerToward`, aimAssist.js:40–49; no velocity lead). See (c).

## (b) Aspects marked works/unknown that need a NEW named live test

- **HUD readout fidelity test (new):** In HELM, hold W then S and screenshot `SupercruiseHud`: assert the log-speed bar fill, the white commanded-pin triangle (lines 122–127), the green drop tick, and — after R to sublight — the bipolar amber-reverse bar (108–116) all track `window._sc.model.{speed,throttle,driveOn}`. No existing recipe exercises the HUD bars; they are asserted only indirectly via model state.
- **DPR/resize test (new):** Mid-flight, resize the window (or emulate a DPR change via devtools device toolbar) and assert the center cross stays at `innerWidth/2, innerHeight/2` and `SupercruiseHud.getLastFrameState()` still renders; catches the resize-only-DPR gap (SupercruiseHud.js:32–41).
- **Pointer-lock-loss test (new):** Start a minimap drag (`_minimapDragging=true`, pointer lock requested at main.js:9801), then press Esc (browser force-exits pointer lock) and release the button. Assert `_minimapDragging` is not stuck. There is **no `pointerlockchange`/`pointerlockerror` handler** (grep 9705/9783/9797/9873/9912 — cleanup only on mouseup), so a browser-initiated lock exit mid-drag has no reset path.
- **ORRERY-burn cancellation test (new):** In non-autopilot ORRERY press `3` (starts a `focusPlanet` burn), then press Escape and hold W/S. Assert whether the pilot stops. Predicted: it does **not** — Escape→`focusPlanet(-1)` (9331 → 6511–6522) calls `cameraController.viewSystem` but never `scPilot.stop()`, and `cameraController.update` is skipped while `scPilot.isActive` (8157), so the leg holds forever with no clean cancel (only M or Z escapes it).
- **Legacy free-look (already `unknown`) — keep, but sharpen:** the audit's recipe is fine; just ensure the middle-mouse peek exclusivity (`scHead` vs `ShipCameraSystem.isFreeLooking`) is asserted in a star system, since that is the only realistic double-fire vector.

## (c) Cross-aspect / reliability-under-repetition risks not surfaced

1. **`celestialTimeMultiplier` × pursuit-only pilot = amplified wedge/non-convergence.** At the default 1.0 (realistic) bodies barely move so the audit's convergence analysis holds. But at a saved high multiplier, moons/planets orbit visibly fast (main.js:6956, 7048), while the pilot steers at the body's *current* position with no lead (aimAssist.js:46) and CRUISE has no timeout (per the audit's leg-motion aspect). A fast-orbiting inner moon can outrun the ship's closing rate → CRUISE limit-cycle → tour freeze. The audit's "55s non-convergence" and "wedge" aspects both omit that Settings can dial this failure in. Negative multipliers (retrograde) also mean the collision-barrier bodies (SupercruiseModel.js:176–189) sweep backward through the pursuit line.

2. **The screensaver's real runtime is a background/occluded tab, where the sim pauses.** `maxStepMs:100` (main.js:6795) + rAF means "runs unattended" is really "runs unattended *only while the foreground/visible tab*." Combined with the nav-sequence's wall-clock `setTimeout` retries (already flagged in the tour cluster) this is not just a jank risk — a genuinely backgrounded screensaver advances the sim at ≤~10% speed while wall-clock timers keep firing, maximizing the drill-down-abort and any timer/sim desync. No aspect tests multi-minute backgrounded endurance and return-to-valid-state (portal idle, `warpEffect` idle, no NaN, `_portalLabState==='idle'`).

3. **Ship code is globally gated OFF (`SHIPS_ENABLED=false`, main.js:152), making a cluster of "suspected issues" non-live.** `shipSpawner.ships` is empty (spawn gated at 4488), so `hitTestBodies` ship-rank (3936), `focusShip`, `_isSameTarget`-returns-false-for-ships, "ships excluded from commit-swap," and "ship burn shows no ETA" are all **latent/dormant**, not shipping-build reachable. The audit repeatedly frames these as live concerns without noting the master gate — reviewers will chase unreachable paths. Worth a single top-level "ship paths dormant" annotation.

4. **Three HELM-entry doors + one persisted `wd_cameraMode` landmine compound over sessions.** The camera cluster flags the persisted-FLIGHT landmine and the three inline entry paths separately; the *interaction* is the risk: quit-in-HELM persists `'flight'` (ShipCameraSystem.js:437), and any future divergence among `_enterFlightInternal` / commit-burn-swap (6309) / tour-takeover (9271) that forgets a resync would surface as an intermittent entry snap only after a specific quit/reload/stop sequence — a classic reliability-under-repetition bug the current per-aspect framing won't catch.

5. **World-origin rebase fires ~every frame at CAP_MAX and the scene-child subtract loop cost scales with system richness.** SupercruiseModel CAP_MAX 20000 u/s → ~333 u/step ≫ the 100-u threshold, so `maybeRebase` (WorldOrigin.js) runs the full top-level-child + tracked-vector subtract loop almost every tick during deep-space cruise. The camera cluster notes this but no aspect measures per-frame rebase cost in a dense system across a long cruise (GC/jitter), nor confirms the reticle/HUD projections (which read `camera` post-rebase) stay stable through the once-per-frame origin shift.

## (d) intendedFunction claims that look unsupported by the code

1. **"Autopilot tour completes a full tour of ALL bodies and re-warps without input" (contract AC8).** The audit's own leg-motion + completion aspects show completion is *count-gated* and any wedged/null-ref leg stalls forever (CRUISE has no timeout; `_stopsVisited` never reaches `queue.length`).
